**225.** 'There is a particle of mahaprasada,' I said, and gladly gave it;
without a second thought the lord put it into his mouth.

আনন্দে নাচয়ে মহা মহেশঠাকুর ।
পদতল-তলে মহী করে দুরদুর ॥ ২২৬ ॥

*ānande nācaẏe mahā maheśaṭhākura |*
*padatala-tale mahī kare duradura || 226 ||*

*Word for word:* anande nachaye — dances in bliss; maha mahesha-thakura — the great lord Mahesha; padatala-tale — under the soles of his feet; mahi kare duradura — the earth shudders

**226.** In bliss the great lord Mahesha dances —
beneath his feet the earth shudders.

প্রেম-ভরে টলমল সুমেরু-পর্বত ।
কম্পমানা বসুমতী চমক সর্বত্র ॥ ২২৭ ॥

*prema-bhare ṭalamala sumeru-parbata |*
*kampamānā basumatī camaka sarbatra || 227 ||*

*Word for word:* prema-bhare — under the weight of prema; talamala — sways; sumeru-parvata — Mount Sumeru; kampamana vasumati — the earth trembles; chamaka sarvatra — alarm everywhere

**227.** Under the weight of prema Mount Sumeru sways,
the earth trembles, alarm is everywhere.

প্রেমে যোগেশ্বর কাঁপে আপনা পাসরে ।
রসাতল যায় মহী মহেশের ভরে ॥ ২২৮ ॥

*preme yogeśbara kāṁpe āpanā pāsare |*
*rasātala yāẏa mahī maheśera bhare || 228 ||*

*Word for word:* preme — in prema; yogeshvara kanpe — the lord of yoga trembles; apana pasare — forgets himself; rasatala yaya mahi — the earth sinks to Rasatala; maheshera bhare — under Mahesha's weight

**228.** The lord of yoga trembles in prema, forgetting himself;
under Mahesha's weight the earth sinks to Rasatala.

অনন্তের ফণা ঠেকে কচ্ছপের পৃষ্ঠে ।
গ্রীবা বক্র করি কূর্ম চাহে একদৃষ্টে ॥ ২২৯ ॥

*anantera phaṇā ṭheke kacchapera pṛṣṭhe |*
*grībā bakra kari kūrma cāhe ekadṛṣṭe || 229 ||*

*Word for word:* anantera phana — Ananta's hoods; theke kachchhapera prishthe — press on the Tortoise's back; griva vakra kari — bending his neck; kurma chahe ekadrishte — Kurma stares fixedly

**229.** Ananta's hoods press against the Tortoise's back;
bending his neck, Kurma stares fixedly [upward].[^04-12]

বক্রগ্রীবা করে ভরে যত দিগ্বাহ ।
হুহুঙ্কার-নাদে ফাটে ব্রহ্মাণ্ড-কটাহ ॥ ২৩০ ॥

*bakragrībā kare bhare yata digbāha |*
*huhuṅkāra-nāde phāṭe brahmāṇḍa-kaṭāha || 230 ||*

*Word for word:* vakra-griva kare — bend their necks; bhare — under the weight; yata digvaha — all the bearers of the quarters; huhunkara-nade — with the roar; phate brahmanda-kataha — the shell of the universe cracks

**230.** Under the weight all the bearers of the quarters bend their necks;[^04-13]
at [Shiva's] roar the shell of the universe cracks.

মহেশের ভর দেবী সহিতে না পারি ।
আস্তে ব্যস্তে গেলা মহেশের পুরী ॥ ২৩১ ॥

*maheśera bhara debī sahite nā pāri |*
*āste byaste gelā maheśera purī || 231 ||*

*Word for word:* maheshera bhara — Mahesha's weight; devi — the goddess [Earth]; sahite na pari — unable to bear; aste vyaste — in haste; gela maheshera puri — went to Mahesha's abode

**231.** Unable to bear Mahesha's weight, the goddess [Earth]
hurried to Mahesha's abode.

কাত্যায়নী-স্থানে মহী কহে করযুড়ি ।
মহেশের নৃত্য-ভরে প্রাণ আমি ছাড়ি ॥ ২৩২ ॥

*kātyāẏanī-sthāne mahī kahe karayuṛi |*
*maheśera nṛtya-bhare prāṇa āmi chāṛi || 232 ||*

*Word for word:* katyayani-sthane — to Katyayani; mahi kahe — the Earth says; karayudi — with joined palms; maheshera nritya-bhare — under the weight of Mahesha's dance; prana ami chhadi — I am giving up my life

**232.** With joined palms the Earth says to Katyayani:
'Under the weight of Mahesha's dance I am giving up my life.

প্রতিকার কর যদি সৃষ্টি রাখিবারে ।
প্রমাদ পড়িল দেখি সকল সংসারে ॥ ২৩৩ ॥

*pratikāra kara yadi sṛṣṭi rākhibāre |*
*pramāda paṛila dekhi sakala saṃsāre || 233 ||*

*Word for word:* pratikara kara — take a remedy; yadi srishti rakhibare — if creation is to be saved; pramada padila dekhi — I see calamity has fallen; sakala samsare — upon the whole world

**233.** Help me, if creation is to be saved:
I see calamity has fallen upon the whole world.'

পৃথিবীর কাতরবাণী শুনিঞা পার্বতী ।
সত্বরে চলিয়া গেলা যথা পশুপতি ॥ ২৩৪ ॥

*pṛthibīra kātarabāṇī śuniñā pārbatī |*
*satbare caliẏā gelā yathā paśupati || 234 ||*

*Word for word:* prithivira katara-vani — the Earth's piteous words; shuniya parvati — hearing, Parvati; satvare chaliya gela — quickly went; yatha pashupati — to where Pashupati was

**234.** Hearing the Earth's piteous words, Parvati
went quickly to where Pashupati was.

পূর্ণ-রসাবেশে নাচে দেবদেবরায় ।
মহেশ-আবেশ ভাঙ্গে কর্কশ কথায় ॥ ২৩৫ ॥

*pūrṇa-rasābeśe nāce debadebarāẏa |*
*maheśa-ābeśa bhāṅge karkaśa kathāẏa || 235 ||*

*Word for word:* purna-rasa-aveshe — fully absorbed in rasa; nache deva-deva-raya — the king of gods dances; mahesha-avesha bhange — she breaks Mahesha's trance; karkasha kathaya — with harsh words

**235.** The king of gods dances fully absorbed in rasa;
with harsh words she breaks Mahesha's rapture.

সম্বিৎ হইলা প্রভু দুঃখিত হইয়া ।
কর্কশ-হৃদয়ে বলে পার্বতী দেখিয়া ॥ ২৩৬ ॥

*sambit hailā prabhu duḥkhita haiẏā |*
*karkaśa-hṛdaẏe bale pārbatī dekhiẏā || 236 ||*

*Word for word:* samvit haila prabhu — the lord came to his senses; duhkhita haiya — grieved; karkasha-hridaye bale — he speaks with a hardened heart; parvati dekhiya — seeing Parvati

**236.** The lord came to his senses, grieved,
and, seeing Parvati, speaks to her harshly:

কি কৈলে কি কৈলে দেবী হেন অবিধান ।
এ আবেশ-ভঙ্গ মোর মরণ সমান ॥ ২৩৭ ॥

*ki kaile ki kaile debī hena abidhāna |*
*e ābeśa-bhaṅga mora maraṇa samāna || 237 ||*

*Word for word:* ki kaile ki kaile — what have you done, what have you done; devi — goddess; hena avidhana — such an impropriety; e avesha-bhanga mora — this breaking of my rapture; marana samana — is like death

**237.** 'What have you done, what have you done, goddess — what an outrage!
To break my rapture is the same as killing me.

তোমা বই রিপু মোর নাহি ত্রিভুবনে ।
এহেন আনন্দ মোর ঘুচাইলে কেনে ॥ ২৩৮ ॥

*tomā bai ripu mora nāhi tribhubane |*
*ehena ānanda mora ghucāile kene || 238 ||*

*Word for word:* toma vai — besides you; ripu mora nahi — I have no enemy; tribhuvane — in the three worlds; ehena ananda mora — such bliss of mine; ghuchaile kene — why did you end?

**238.** I have no enemy in the three worlds but you:
why did you end such bliss of mine?'

শুনিঞা কাতরে দেবী বোলে আরবার ।
পৃথিবী দেখহ প্রভু সম্মুখে তোমার ॥ ২৩৯ ॥

*śuniñā kātare debī bole ārabāra |*
*pṛthibī dekhaha prabhu sammukhe tomāra || 239 ||*

*Word for word:* shuniya — hearing; katare devi bole — the goddess says piteously; arabara — again; prithivi dekhaha — look at the Earth; prabhu — lord; sammukhe tomara — before you

**239.** Hearing this, the goddess says piteously again:
'Look, lord, at the Earth before you.

তব পদ-তল-ছলে যায় রসাতল ।
সৃষ্টি নষ্ট হয় তেঞি বৈলুঁ কটূত্তর ॥ ২৪০ ॥

*taba pada-tala-chale yāẏa rasātala |*
*sṛṣṭi naṣṭa haẏa teñi bailuṁ kaṭūttara || 240 ||*

*Word for word:* taba pada-tala-chhale — under the stamping of your feet; yaya rasatala — she sinks to Rasatala; srishti nashta haya — creation is perishing; tenji bailun katu-uttara — that is why I spoke harshly

**240.** Under the stamping of your feet she is sinking to Rasatala,
creation is perishing — that is why I spoke harshly.

অপরাধ কৈলুঁ দোষ ক্ষম মহাশয় ।
হাসিয়া মহেশ দিলা পৃথিবী-বিদায় ॥ ২৪১ ॥

*aparādha kailuṁ doṣa kṣama mahāśaẏa |*
*hāsiẏā maheśa dilā pṛthibī-bidāẏa || 241 ||*

*Word for word:* aparadha kailun — I have offended; dosha kshama — forgive the fault; mahashaya — great one; hasiya mahesha — smiling, Mahesha; dila prithivi-vidaya — dismissed the Earth

**241.** I have offended — forgive my fault, great one.'
Smiling, Mahesha dismissed the Earth.

পুনরপি পুছে দেবী মিনতি করিয়া ।
এক নিবেদিয়ে প্রভু সন্দেহ লাগিয়া ॥ ২৪২ ॥

*punarapi puche debī minati kariẏā |*
*eka nibediẏe prabhu sandeha lāgiẏā || 242 ||*

*Word for word:* punarapi puchhe devi — again the goddess asks; minati kariya — entreating; eka nivediye — I ask one thing; prabhu — lord; sandeha lagiya — because of a doubt

**242.** And again the goddess asks entreatingly:
'Lord, I ask one thing — a doubt troubles me:

কৃষ্ণরসাবেশে তুমি নাচ প্রতিদিনে ।
আজি মহী রসাতল যায় কি কারণে ॥ ২৪৩ ॥

*kṛṣṇarasābeśe tumi nāca pratidine |*
*āji mahī rasātala yāẏa ki kāraṇe || 243 ||*

*Word for word:* krishna-rasa-aveshe — absorbed in the rasa of Krishna; tumi nacha pratidine — you dance every day; aji — today; mahi rasatala yaya — the earth sinks to Rasatala; ki karane — for what reason

**243.** every day you dance absorbed in the rasa of Krishna —
why then does the earth sink to Rasatala today?

কোটি-দিবাকর-তেজঃ কিরণ প্রচণ্ড ।
অতি অপরূপ তেজঃ না ধরে ব্রহ্মাণ্ড ॥ ২৪৪ ॥

*koṭi-dibākara-tejaḥ kiraṇa pracaṇḍa |*
*ati aparūpa tejaḥ nā dhare brahmāṇḍa || 244 ||*

*Word for word:* koti-divakara-tejah — the splendour of millions of suns; kirana prachanda — fierce rays; ati aparupa tejah — most wondrous radiance; na dhare brahmanda — the universe cannot hold

**244.** The splendour of millions of suns, fierce rays —
the universe cannot hold so wondrous a radiance.

আজি কেনে অপরূপ আনন্দ অনন্ত ।
সবিশেষ কহ মোরে প্রভু গুণবন্ত ॥ ২৪৫ ॥

*āji kene aparūpa ānanda ananta |*
*sabiśeṣa kaha more prabhu guṇabanta || 245 ||*

*Word for word:* aji kene — why today; aparupa ananda ananta — wondrous, endless bliss; savishesha kaha more — tell me in detail; prabhu gunavanta — virtuous lord

**245.** Why this wondrous, endless bliss today?
Tell me in detail, lord, rich in virtues.'

মহেশ কহয়ে—শুন আনন্দ-কাহিনী ।
প্রভুর প্রসাদ মোরে দিল মহামুনি ॥ ২৪৬ ॥

*maheśa kahaẏe—śuna ānanda-kāhinī |*
*prabhura prasāda more dila mahāmuni || 246 ||*

*Word for word:* mahesha kahaye — Mahesha says; shuna ananda-kahini — hear a joyful tale; prabhura prasada — the Lord's prasada; more dila mahamuni — the great sage gave me

**246.** Mahesha says: 'Hear a joyful tale:
the great sage gave me the Lord's prasada.

দুর্লভ এ ত্রিজগতে বিষ্ণু-নিবেদিত ।
বিশেষ অধরামৃত বেদে অবিদিত ॥ ২৪৭ ॥

*durlabha e trijagate biṣṇu-nibedita |*
*biśeṣa adharāmṛta bede abidita || 247 ||*

*Word for word:* durlabha — rare; e trijagate — in these three worlds; vishnu-nivedita — what is offered to Vishnu; vishesha — still more; adhara-amrita — the nectar of His lips; vede avidita — unknown to the Vedas

**247.** Rare in the three worlds is [a taste of] what is offered to Vishnu,
still more the nectar of His lips, unknown to the Vedas.[^04-14]

হেন মহাপ্রসাদ আমি করিনু ভক্ষণ ।
সফল জনম মোর আজি শুভক্ষণ ॥ ২৪৮ ॥

*hena mahāprasāda āmi karinu bhakṣaṇa |*
*saphala janama mora āji śubhakṣaṇa || 248 ||*

*Word for word:* hena mahaprasada — such mahaprasada; ami karinu bhakshana — I have eaten; saphala janama mora — my birth is fruitful; aji shubhakshana — today is an auspicious hour

**248.** Such mahaprasada I have eaten —
my birth is fruitful, this is an auspicious hour.'

নারদ-প্রসাদে মহাপ্রসাদ-পরশ ।
কহিল মঙ্গল কথা সম্পদ সরস ॥ ২৪৯ ॥

*nārada-prasāde mahāprasāda-paraśa |*
*kahila maṅgala kathā sampada sarasa || 249 ||*

*Word for word:* narada-prasade — by Narada's grace; mahaprasada-parasha — the touch of mahaprasada; kahila mangala katha — he told the auspicious story; sampada sarasa — a delightful treasure

**249.** By Narada's grace — the touch of mahaprasada:
he told her this auspicious story, a delightful treasure.

শুনি ঠাকুরের বাণী কহে মহামায়া ।
এতদিনে জানিল তোমার যত দয়া ॥ ২৫০ ॥

*śuni ṭhākurera bāṇī kahe mahāmāẏā |*
*etadine jānila tomāra yata daẏā || 250 ||*

*Word for word:* shuni thakurera vani — hearing the lord's words; kahe mahamaya — Mahamaya says; etadine janila — now at last I know; tomara yata daya — how great is your kindness

**250.** Hearing the lord's words, Mahamaya says:[^04-15]
'Now at last I know how great your kindness is!

অর্ধ অঙ্গে ধর মোরে সকলি কপট ।
কৈতব পিরীতি এবে হইল প্রকট ॥ ২৫১ ॥

*ardha aṅge dhara more sakali kapaṭa |*
*kaitaba pirīti ebe haila prakaṭa || 251 ||*

*Word for word:* ardha ange dhara more — you hold me as half your body; sakali kapata — it is all deceit; kaitava piriti — false love; ebe haila prakata — now is exposed

**251.** You hold me as half your body — it is all deceit;
now your false love is exposed!

এহেন দুর্লভ মহাপ্রসাদ পাইয়া ।
একেলা ভুঞ্জিলা দেব আমারে না দিয়া ॥ ২৫২ ॥

*ehena durlabha mahāprasāda pāiẏā |*
*ekelā bhuñjilā deba āmāre nā diẏā || 252 ||*

*Word for word:* ehena durlabha mahaprasada — such rare mahaprasada; paiya — having got; ekela bhunjila — you ate alone; deva — O god; amare na diya — without giving me

**252.** Having got such rare mahaprasada,
you, god, ate it alone without giving me any!'

লজ্জায় অবশ হঞা বোলে শূলপাণি ।
এ ধনের অধিকারী নহ তুমি ভবানী ॥ ২৫৩ ॥

*lajjāẏa abaśa hañā bole śūlapāṇi |*
*e dhanera adhikārī naha tumi bhabānī || 253 ||*

*Word for word:* lajjaya avasha haina — helpless with shame; bole shulapani — the Trident-bearer says; e dhanera adhikari — entitled to this treasure; naha tumi bhavani — you are not, Bhavani

**253.** Helpless with shame, the Trident-bearer says:
'This treasure is not for you, Bhavani.'

শুনিঞা রুষিলা হিয়া বোলে আদ্যাশক্তি ।
বৈষ্ণবী নাম মোর করি বিষ্ণুভক্তি ॥ ২৫৪ ॥

*śuniñā ruṣilā hiẏā bole ādyāśakti |*
*baiṣṇabī nāma mora kari biṣṇubhakti || 254 ||*

*Word for word:* shuniya — hearing; rushila hiya — angered at heart; bole adya-shakti — the primal Shakti says; vaishnavi nama mora — my name is Vaishnavi; kari vishnu-bhakti — I practise devotion to Vishnu

**254.** Hearing this, angered, the primal Shakti says:
'My name is Vaishnavi; I serve Vishnu.

প্রতিজ্ঞা করিলুঁ মুঞি সভার ভিতরে ।
জানিবে আমারে দয়া প্রভুর অন্তরে ॥ ২৫৫ ॥

*pratijñā kariluṁ muñi sabhāra bhitare |*
*jānibe āmāre daẏā prabhura antare || 255 ||*

*Word for word:* pratijna karilun munji — I make a vow; sabhara bhitare — before all; janibe — you will know; amare daya — the kindness towards me; prabhura antare — in the Lord's heart

**255.** I make a vow before all —
and you will know whether there is kindness for me in the Lord's heart:

এই মহাপ্রসাদ মুঞি দিমু জগতেরে ।
মোর প্রতিজ্ঞায় পাবে শৃগাল-কুক্কুরে ॥ ২৫৬ ॥

*ei mahāprasāda muñi dimu jagatere |*
*mora pratijñāẏa pābe śṛgāla-kukkure || 256 ||*

*Word for word:* ei mahaprasada — this mahaprasada; munji dimu jagatere — I shall give to the world; mora pratijnaya — by my vow; pabe shrigala-kukkure — even jackals and dogs will receive it

**256.** this mahaprasada I shall give to the whole world —
by my vow even jackals and dogs will receive it.'[^04-16]

এছন প্রতিজ্ঞা কাত্যায়নী যবে কৈলা ।
শুনিঞা বৈকুণ্ঠনাথ সত্বরে আইলা ॥ ২৫৭ ॥

*echana pratijñā kātyāẏanī yabe kailā |*
*śuniñā baikuṇṭhanātha satbare āilā || 257 ||*

*Word for word:* echhana pratijna — such a vow; katyayani yabe kaila — when Katyayani made; shuniya — hearing; vaikuntha-natha — the Lord of Vaikuntha; satvare aila — came quickly

**257.** When Katyayani made such a vow,
the Lord of Vaikuntha, hearing it, came quickly.

সম্ভ্রমে উঠিয়া দেবী কৈল পরণাম ।
নিবেদন কৈল দেবী সজল-নয়ান ॥ ২৫৮ ॥

*sambhrame uṭhiẏā debī kaila paraṇāma |*
*nibedana kaila debī sajala-naẏāna || 258 ||*

*Word for word:* sambhrame uthiya — rising respectfully; devi kaila paranama — the goddess bowed; nivedana kaila devi — the goddess made her plea; sajala-nayana — with tearful eyes

**258.** Rising respectfully, the goddess bowed
and with tearful eyes made her plea to Him;

কাতর-অন্তরে কহে ছাড়িয়া নিঃশ্বাস ।
আনন্দ-হৃদয়ে কহে এ লোচনদাস ॥ ২৫৯ ॥

*kātara-antare kahe chāṛiẏā niḥśbāsa |*
*ānanda-hṛdaẏe kahe e locanadāsa || 259 ||*

*Word for word:* katara-antare kahe — she speaks with an aching heart; chhadiya nihshvasa — sighing; ananda-hridaye — with a joyful heart; kahe e lochanadasa — says this Lochana Dasa

**259.** with an aching heart, sighing, she speaks —
and with a joyful heart this Lochana Dasa tells it.

*Raga vibhasha*

বোলে পঁহু লহু বোলে, নহ দেবী উতরোলে,
একি হয় তোর ব্যবহার ।
তোর মায়া-বন্ধে অন্ধ, সকল সংসার-খণ্ড,
তেঞি সৃষ্টি আছয়ে আমার ॥ ২৬০ ॥

*bole paṁhu lahu bole, naha debī utarole,*
*eki haẏa tora byabahāra |*
*tora māẏā-bandhe andha, sakala saṃsāra-khaṇḍa,*
*teñi sṛṣṭi āchaẏe āmāra || 260 ||*

*Word for word:* bole panhu — the Lord says; lahu bole — in soft words; naha devi utarole — do not be agitated, goddess; eki haya tora vyavahara — what kind of conduct is this; tora maya-bandhe andha — blind in the bonds of your maya; sakala samsara-khanda — is the whole world; tenji — therefore; srishti achhaye amara — My creation goes on

**260.** Softly the Lord says: 'Do not be agitated, goddess;
what is this conduct of yours?
The whole world is blind in the bonds of your maya —
that is why My creation goes on.

তুমি মোর আদ্যাশক্তি, তুমি সে জানহ ভক্তি,
তুমি মোর প্রকৃতিস্বরূপা ।
আমি তোমা বহি নহি, তুমি আমা বহি কহি,
যে করহ তোমারি সে কৃপা ॥ ২৬১ ॥

*tumi mora ādyāśakti, tumi se jānaha bhakti,*
*tumi mora prakṛtisbarūpā |*
*āmi tomā bahi nahi, tumi āmā bahi kahi,*
*ye karaha tomāri se kṛpā || 261 ||*

*Word for word:* tumi mora adya-shakti — you are My primal shakti; tumi se janaha bhakti — you know bhakti; tumi mora prakriti-svarupa — you are My prakriti in essence; ami toma vahi nahi — I am not apart from you; tumi ama vahi kahi — [nor] you, I say, apart from Me; ye karaha — whatever you do; tomari se kripa — is your grace

**261.** You are My primal shakti, you know bhakti,
you are by nature My prakriti;
I am not apart from you, nor, I say, are you apart from Me;[^04-17]
whatever you do is your grace.

হরগৌরী-আরাধনে, সর্বলোক আমা জানে,
হরগৌরী মোর আত্মতনু ।
তোর পরসন্ন হিয়া, ঘুচিল সকল মায়া,
ঘুচিল স্ব-পর-ভেদ ভিনু ॥ ২৬২ ॥

*haragaurī-ārādhane, sarbaloka āmā jāne,*
*haragaurī mora ātmatanu |*
*tora parasanna hiẏā, ghucila sakala māẏā,*
*ghucila sba-para-bheda bhinu || 262 ||*

*Word for word:* hara-gauri-aradhane — by worship of Hara and Gauri; sarvaloka ama jane — all people know Me; hara-gauri mora atma-tanu — Hara and Gauri are My own body; tora parasanna hiya — your heart being pleased; ghuchila sakala maya — all maya is gone; ghuchila sva-para-bheda bhinu — the division of "mine" and "another's" is gone

**262.** By worshipping Hara and Gauri all people come to know Me:
Hara and Gauri are My own body;
when your heart is pleased, all maya vanishes,
the division into 'mine' and 'another's' vanishes.[^04-18]

এছন প্রতিজ্ঞা তোর, এহেন উচ্ছিষ্ট মোর,
অবিরোধে দিবে সভাকারে ।
মহাপ্রসাদের গন্ধে, সভে হবে মুক্তবন্ধে,
ঘুচাইবে নির্বন্ধ বিচারে ॥ ২৬৩ ॥

*echana pratijñā tora, ehena ucchiṣṭa mora,*
*abirodhe dibe sabhākāre |*
*mahāprasādera gandhe, sabhe habe muktabandhe,*
*ghucāibe nirbandha bicāre || 263 ||*

*Word for word:* echhana pratijna tora — such is your vow; ehena uchchhishta mora — such remnants of Mine; avirodhe dibe sabhakare — you will give to all without hindrance; mahaprasadera gandhe — by the fragrance of mahaprasada; sabhe habe mukta-bandhe — all will be freed from bonds; ghuchaibe nirbandha vichare — it will end restrictive considerations

**263.** Such is your vow — these remnants of Mine
you will give to all without hindrance;
by the mere fragrance of mahaprasada all will be freed from bonds;
it will do away with restrictive rules.

শুনিঞা ঠাকুর-বাণী, পুন কহে কাত্যায়নী,
মোরে যদি দয়া আছে চিতে ।
অবশ্য উচ্ছিষ্ট দিবে, ভুঞ্জিবে সকল জীবে,
অবিরোধে পাবে ত্রিজগতে ॥ ২৬৪ ॥

*śuniñā ṭhākura-bāṇī, puna kahe kātyāẏanī,*
*more yadi daẏā āche cite |*
*abaśya ucchiṣṭa dibe, bhuñjibe sakala jībe,*
*abirodhe pābe trijagate || 264 ||*

*Word for word:* shuniya thakura-vani — hearing the Lord's words; puna kahe katyayani — Katyayani says again; more yadi daya achhe chite — if there is kindness for me in [Your] heart; avashya uchchhishta dibe — surely give the remnants; bhunjibe sakala jive — all beings will eat; avirodhe pabe trijagate — the three worlds will receive without hindrance

**264.** Hearing the Lord's words, Katyayani says again:
'If there is kindness for me in Your heart,
surely give [Your] remnants: let all beings eat them,
let the three worlds receive them without hindrance.'

পুন কহে গুণমণি, শুন দেবী কাত্যায়নি,
প্রতিজ্ঞা পালিব আছে কথা ।
পুরুব-রহস্য এই, তোমারে নিভৃতে কই,
ঘুচিবে সংসার-জ্বর-চিন্তা ॥ ২৬৫ ॥

*puna kahe guṇamaṇi, śuna debī kātyāẏani,*
*pratijñā pāliba āche kathā |*
*puruba-rahasya ei, tomāre nibhṛte kai,*
*ghucibe saṃsāra-jbara-cintā || 265 ||*

*Word for word:* puna kahe gunamani — the Jewel of virtues says again; shuna devi katyayani — hear, goddess Katyayani; pratijna paliba — I shall keep [your] vow; achhe katha — there is a story; puruba-rahasya ei — this is an ancient secret; tomare nibhrite kai — I tell you privately; ghuchibe samsara-jvara-chinta — the anxiety of the fever of worldly life will end

**265.** Again the Jewel of virtues says: 'Hear, goddess Katyayani:
I shall keep your vow — there is a story about it;
it is an ancient secret; I tell it to you privately —
and the anxiety of the fever of worldly life will go.

পুরুব-রহস্য যত, কেহ নাহি জানে তত্ত্ব,
সমুদ্র মথিল দেবগণে ।
মন্দার মথন-দণ্ড, রজ্জু ফণী অনন্ত,
লোম উপজিল ঘরিষণে ॥ ২৬৬ ॥

*puruba-rahasya yata, keha nāhi jāne tattba,*
*samudra mathila debagaṇe |*
*mandāra mathana-daṇḍa, rajju phaṇī ananta,*
*loma upajila ghariṣaṇe || 266 ||*

*Word for word:* puruba-rahasya yata — of this ancient secret; keha nahi jane tattva — no one knows the truth; samudra mathila deva-gane — the gods churned the ocean; mandara mathana-danda — Mandara the churning rod; rajju phani ananta — the serpent Ananta the rope; loma upajila gharishane — from the friction a hair (shoot) arose

**266.** No one knows the truth of this ancient secret:
when the gods churned the ocean —
Mandara the churning rod, the serpent Ananta the rope —
from the friction a shoot arose.[^04-19]

সে মোর কল্পতরু, যাচক যাচিঞা করু,
যার যত যেই মনে বাসে ।
যে জন যে ধন চাহে, সে জন সে ধন পাহে,
বিমুখ না করে প্রতি-আশে ॥ ২৬৭ ॥

*se mora kalpataru, yācaka yāciñā karu,*
*yāra yata yei mane bāse |*
*ye jana ye dhana cāhe, se jana se dhana pāhe,*
*bimukha nā kare prati-āśe || 267 ||*

*Word for word:* se mora kalpa-taru — that is My wish-fulfilling tree; yachaka yachina karu — let suppliants ask; yara yata yei mane vase — whatever each holds in mind; ye jana ye dhana chahe — whoever wants whatever wealth; se jana se dhana pahe — he gets that wealth; vimukha na kare prati-ashe — it turns none away from his hope

**267.** That is My wish-fulfilling tree: let suppliants ask
whatever each holds in mind;
whoever wants whatever treasure receives that treasure —
it disappoints no one in his hope.

তহিঁ এক দিব্য তেজে, চারু তরুবর-মাঝে,
শ্রীচৈতন্য অধিষ্ঠিত দেহে ।
সে মোর সহজ রূপ, কেবল করুণা-ভূপ,
আর যত সেহ সম নহে ॥ ২৬৮ ॥

*tahiṁ eka dibya teje, cāru tarubara-mājhe,*
*śrīcaitanya adhiṣṭhita dehe |*
*se mora sahaja rūpa, kebala karuṇā-bhūpa,*
*āra yata seha sama nahe || 268 ||*

*Word for word:* tahin eka divya teje — there, in a divine radiance; charu taruvara-majhe — within the beautiful tree; shri-chaitanya adhishthita dehe — Sri Chaitanya is present embodied; se mora sahaja rupa — that is My natural form; kevala karuna-bhupa — a king of pure compassion; ara yata — all others; seha sama nahe — are not equal to Him

**268.** There, in a divine radiance, within that beautiful tree,
Sri Chaitanya is present in bodily form;[^04-20]
that is My natural form, a king of pure compassion —
all others are not equal to Him.

যত যত অবতার, সেই সে আশ্রয়াগার,
লীলা-কলা-বিলাসের তরে ।
পৃথিবীতে রহিব আমি, ত্রিজগত-নাথ-স্বামী,
করুণা করিব পরচারে ॥ ২৬৯ ॥

*yata yata abatāra, sei se āśraẏāgāra,*
*līlā-kalā-bilāsera tare |*
*pṛthibīte rahiba āmi, trijagata-nātha-sbāmī,*
*karuṇā kariba paracāre || 269 ||*

*Word for word:* yata yata avatara — all the avataras; sei se ashrayagara — He is their abode and shelter; lila-kala-vilasera tare — for pastimes, arts and enjoyment; prithivite rahiba ami — I shall remain on earth; trijagata-natha-svami — Lord and master of the three worlds; karuna kariba parachare — I shall spread mercy

**269.** All the avataras — He is their abode and shelter,[^04-21]
[from Him they come] for the sake of pastimes, arts and delights.
I shall remain on earth, Lord and master of the three worlds,
and shall spread mercy.

কলিযুগে সবিশেষে, সঙ্কীর্তন-পরকাশে,
হব আমি মনুজ-মূরতি ।
তনু হব হেম-গৌর, প্রতিজ্ঞা পালিব তোর,
প্রচারিব পরম পিরীতি ॥ ২৭০ ॥

*kaliyuge sabiśeṣe, saṅkīrtana-parakāśe,*
*haba āmi manuja-mūrati |*
*tanu haba hema-gaura, pratijñā pāliba tora,*
*pracāriba parama pirīti || 270 ||*

*Word for word:* kali-yuge savisheshe — especially in the Kali-yuga; sankirtana-parakashe — revealing sankirtana; haba ami manuja-murati — I shall take a human form; tanu haba hema-gaura — My body will be golden; pratijna paliba tora — I shall keep your vow; prachariba parama piriti — I shall spread the highest love

**270.** Especially in the Kali-yuga, revealing sankirtana,
I shall take a human form;
My body will be golden; I shall keep your vow
and spread the highest love.

এ মোর অন্তর-হিয়া, তোমারে কহিল ইহা,
সম্বরি রাখহ নিজমনে ।
সব-অবতার-সার, কলি-গোরা-অবতার,
নিস্তারিব লোক নিজগুণে ॥ ২৭১ ॥

*e mora antara-hiẏā, tomāre kahila ihā,*
*sambari rākhaha nijamane |*
*saba-abatāra-sāra, kali-gorā-abatāra,*
*nistāriba loka nijaguṇe || 271 ||*

*Word for word:* e mora antara-hiya — this is the secret of My heart; tomare kahila iha — I have told you; sambari rakhaha nija-mane — keep it guarded in your mind; saba-avatara-sara — the essence of all avataras; kali-gora-avatara — the avatara Gora in Kali; nistariba loka nija-gune — I shall deliver people by My virtues

**271.** This secret of My heart I have told you —
keep it guarded in your mind:
the essence of all avataras, Gora, the avatara of Kali —
by My virtues I shall deliver the people.'"

বিষ্ণু-কাত্যায়নী-সনে, সংবাদ ব্রহ্মপুরাণে,
উৎকলখণ্ডেতে পরকাশ ।
রাজা সে প্রতাপরুদ্র, সর্বগুণের সমুদ্র,
ব্যক্ত কৈল অনেক প্রকাশ ॥ ২৭২ ॥

*biṣṇu-kātyāẏanī-sane, saṃbāda brahmapurāṇe,*
*utkalakhaṇḍete parakāśa |*
*rājā se pratāparudra, sarbaguṇera samudra,*
*byakta kaila aneka prakāśa || 272 ||*

*Word for word:* vishnu-katyayani-sane samvada — the dialogue of Vishnu with Katyayani; brahma-purane — in the Brahma-purana; utkala-khandete parakasha — is set forth in the Utkala-khanda; raja se prataparudra — King Prataparudra; sarva-gunera samudra — an ocean of all virtues; vyakta kaila aneka prakasha — made it widely known

**272.** The dialogue of Vishnu with Katyayani is in the *Brahma-purana*,
set forth in the *Utkala-khanda*;
King Prataparudra, an ocean of all virtues,
made it widely known.[^04-22]

এ কথা তোমার মনে, স্মরণ নাহিক কেনে,
হাসি হাসি বোলে মুনিরাজে ।
প্রভু আজ্ঞা দিল মোরে, ঘোষণা দিবার তরে,
কলিযুগ-অবতার-কাজে ॥ ২৭৩ ॥

*e kathā tomāra mane, smaraṇa nāhika kene,*
*hāsi hāsi bole munirāje |*
*prabhu ājñā dila more, ghoṣaṇā dibāra tare,*
*kaliyuga-abatāra-kāje || 273 ||*

*Word for word:* e katha tomara mane — this in your mind; smarana nahika kene — why do you not remember; hasi hasi bole muniraje — laughing, says the king of sages; prabhu ajna dila more — the Lord ordered me; ghoshana dibara tare — to proclaim; kali-yuga-avatara-kaje — the work of the avatara of the Kali-yuga

**273.** "Why do you not remember this?" —
laughing, says the king of sages. —
"The Lord ordered me to proclaim
the work of the avatara of the Kali-yuga:

সভে কলিযুগ পাঞা, পৃথ্বীতে জনম গিয়া,
নাম-বিপর্যয় নিজ অংশে ।
সেই সব লোকনাথ, সব-পারিষদ-সাথ,
জনম লভিব বিপ্রবংশে ॥ ২৭৪ ॥

*sabhe kaliyuga pāñā, pṛthbīte janama giẏā,*
*nāma-biparyaẏa nija aṃśe |*
*sei saba lokanātha, saba-pāriṣada-sātha,*
*janama labhiba biprabaṃśe || 274 ||*

*Word for word:* sabhe kali-yuga pana — all of you, when the Kali-yuga comes; prithvite janama giya — taking birth on earth; nama-viparyaya — with changed names; nija amshe — as your own portions; sei saba loka-natha — all those lords of the worlds; saba-parishada-satha — with all the associates; janama labhiba vipra-vamshe — will be born in brahmana families

**274.** when the Kali-yuga comes, all of you will be born on earth
as your own portions, under other names;[^04-23]
all those lords of the worlds, with all the associates,
will be born in brahmana families."

শুনিঞা নারদ-বাণী, উল্লসিত শূলপাণি,
উল্লসিতা দেবী কাত্যায়নী ।
আনন্দে ভরল পুরী, সভে বোলে হরি হরি,
উঠিল আনন্দ-রোল-ধ্বনি ॥ ২৭৫ ॥

*śuniñā nārada-bāṇī, ullasita śūlapāṇi,*
*ullasitā debī kātyāẏanī |*
*ānande bharala purī, sabhe bole hari hari,*
*uṭhila ānanda-rola-dhbani || 275 ||*

*Word for word:* shuniya narada-vani — hearing Narada's words; ullasita shulapani — the Trident-bearer rejoiced; ullasita devi katyayani — the goddess Katyayani rejoiced; anande bharala puri — the abode filled with joy; sabhe bole hari hari — all say "Hari, Hari"; uthila ananda-rola-dhvani — a joyful clamour arose

**275.** Hearing Narada's words, the Trident-bearer rejoiced,
the goddess Katyayani rejoiced;
the abode filled with joy, all say "Hari, Hari!" —
a joyful clamour arose.

[^04-1]: A reference to the source of the dialogue, the *Jaimini-bharata* (v. 155). Which text by this name Lochana Dasa has in mind is unclear.
[^04-2]: *Malasat*: slapping the shoulders and thighs with the palms, as wrestlers do to challenge an opponent; in the Gaudiya biographies one of the signs of ecstatic rapture.
[^04-3]: Narada humbly names the grace of Katyayani (Parvati) and Shiva as the source of his devotion. For Gaudiya Vaishnavas Shiva is the best of Vaishnavas (*Bhag.* 12.13.16); so Bhaktisiddhanta also calls him in his summary of this section.
[^04-4]: Nandi and Mahakala are Shiva's servants and doorkeepers.
[^04-5]: V. 172+1 is found only in the 1983 edition; in the 1903 edition it is in a footnote, as an additional reading of one printed book. In the 1983 edition the first line of v. 172 also differs: "He embraces [him] tightly with joy in his heart" — without the words "seated him beside himself". The text does not say who leads Narada — Shiva or the goddess.
[^04-6]: The conversation of Uddhava with the Lord before His departure is in the *Bhagavata*, canto 11 (11.6.43–50 and the following *Uddhava-gita*, where the Lord explains yoga). Literally "explained yoga concerning His own doings".
[^04-7]: Cf. the *Bhagavad-gita*, chs. 7 and 10. The Lord pervades everything by His energies and dwells in all as the Paramatma, while remaining a person distinct from creation and inconceivably one with it (*achintya-bhedabheda*); there is no identification of God with the world here.
[^04-8]: In Bhaktisiddhanta's edition every quoted shloka is followed by his prose order of the words (*anvaya*) and a Bengali translation; on this page they are almost illegible. "Your maya" is the external energy of the Lord, which holds living beings captive; the Lord Himself is not subject to it.
[^04-9]: "Hari's servant" (*hari-dasa*) here is Uddhava.
[^04-10]: "The Great Lord" (*mahaprabhu*) here is Narayana, the Lord of Vaikuntha, not Sri Chaitanya.
[^04-11]: Sudarshana is the Lord's disc, the guardian of His apartments; the Lord wonders whether he has offended Lakshmi.
[^04-12]: The earth is upheld beneath by the serpent Ananta (Shesha) on his hoods, and beneath him by the Tortoise (Kurma).
[^04-13]: "The bearers of the quarters" (*digvaha*): the *diggajas*, the elephants said to support the world in the eight directions.
[^04-14]: "The nectar of His lips" (*adharamrita*): the remnants of food touched by the Lord's lips; this is mahaprasada in the proper sense.
[^04-15]: Mahamaya is a name of Parvati (Durga). For Gaudiya Vaishnavas Durga is the external energy of the Lord, carrying out His will as a shadow follows the movements of the body (*Brahma-samhita* 5.44); below the Lord Himself calls her His shakti (vv. 260–261).
[^04-16]: Cf. the tradition of Puri: everything offered to Jagannatha is then offered to Vimala-devi (Parvati) in Jagannatha's temple, and only then becomes the mahaprasada that is given to all without distinction.
[^04-17]: An energy is inseparable from its possessor (*shakti* and *shaktiman*). In the Gaudiya understanding Durga is the external energy of the Lord (*bahiranga-shakti*, maya), the shadow of His internal energy (*chit-shakti*) to which Radha and the eternal consorts belong; the Lord Himself is not subject to maya — she serves His will, keeping captive those who have turned from Him.
[^04-18]: So Lochana Dasa: "Hara and Gauri are My own body." According to Gaudiya Vaishnava teaching Shiva is not different from the Lord in source, but, in contact with tamo-guna, becomes distinct, as milk turned into curd (*Brahma-samhita* 5.45); Durga is the Lord's external energy (5.44). "The division into mine and another's" is the false "I" and "mine" (cf. v. 35) created by maya; there is no question of the difference between the soul and God disappearing.
[^04-19]: Literally "a hair" (*loma*); from the following verses, the shoot from which the wish-fulfilling tree (*kalpa-taru*) grew (cf. the Parijata, which came out of the churned ocean).
[^04-20]: Lochana Dasa probably connects this tree with the Kalpa-vata, the sacred banyan by Jagannatha's temple in Puri, honoured as a wish-fulfilling tree; the whole dialogue (v. 272) comes from the traditions of Utkala (Orissa) and Purushottama-kshetra.
[^04-21]: Cf. *Chaitanya-charitamrita*, Adi 2: Krishna (and Gaura as Krishna) is the *avatari*, the source of all avataras.
[^04-22]: The *Utkala-khanda* is the account of Purushottama-kshetra (Puri) known as part of the *Skanda-purana*; a Purushottama account is also found in the *Brahma-purana*. Prataparudra was the king of Orissa (reigned c. 1497–1540), a devotee of Sri Chaitanya. What exactly Prataparudra did to spread this account is not clear from the text.
[^04-23]: Cf. Kavi Karnapura's *Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika*, which states which eternal associates and gods appeared as whom in Gaura-lila. The words "in brahmana families" are the author's generalization: not all the Lord's associates were brahmanas by birth (Murari Gupta, for example, was a vaidya, and Haridasa Thakura was born in a Muslim family).

---

# Sutra-khanda, part 5 (portion 05)

*Narada comes to Brahma and gives him the Lord's words about His appearance in the Kali-yuga; Brahma tells of the doubt of Sanaka and the other Kumaras, of the Lord's answer in four verses, and of how the* Bhagavata *was given through Narada; Brahma recalls Garga Muni's words about the colours of the avataras in the various yugas and, following the* Bhagavata, *describes the avataras and the worship of the Satya-, Treta- and Dvapara-yugas*

চলিলা নারদমুনি, উঠিল বীণার ধ্বনি,
সে স্বর-মধুর-রস-সিঞ্চে ।
অমিয়া-মধুর-ধারা, শ্রবণে পূরিল পারা,
ত্রিভুবন-জন-মন রঞ্জে ॥ ২৭৬ ॥

*calilā nāradamuni, uṭhila bīṇāra dhbani,*
*se sbara-madhura-rasa-siñce |*
*amiẏā-madhura-dhārā, śrabaṇe pūrila pārā,*
*tribhubana-jana-mana rañje || 276 ||*

*Word for word:* chalila naradamuni — the sage Narada went; uthila vinara dhvani — the sound of the vina rose; se svara-madhura-rasa-sinche — that sound sprinkles sweet rasa; amiya-madhura-dhara — a sweet stream of nectar; shravane purila para — as if filling the ears; tribhuvana-jana-mana ranje — delights the hearts of the people of the three worlds

**276.** The sage Narada went on, his vina sounding —
its sound sprinkles sweet rasa;
as if a stream of sweet nectar filled the ears,
delighting the hearts of the people of the three worlds.

আপনা পাসরে যাইতে, চলিতে না পারে পথে,
অনুরাগে অরুণ-বদন ।
না জানিল পথশ্রম, ভালে বিন্দু বিন্দু ঘর্ম,
উপনীত ব্রহ্মার সদন ॥ ২৭৭ ॥

*āpanā pāsare yāite, calite nā pāre pathe,*
*anurāge aruṇa-badana |*
*nā jānila pathaśrama, bhāle bindu bindu gharma,*
*upanīta brahmāra sadana || 277 ||*

*Word for word:* apana pasare yaite — going, he forgets himself; chalite na pare pathe — cannot walk on the road; anurage aruna-vadana — face reddened with love; na janila patha-shrama — he felt no weariness of the road; bhale bindu bindu gharma — drops of sweat on his brow; upanita brahmara sadana — he reached Brahma's abode

**277.** Going, he forgets himself, he cannot keep to the road,
his face reddened with love;
he feels no weariness of the way, drops of sweat on his brow —
and so he reached Brahma's abode.

দেখি ব্রহ্মা অতি ব্যস্তে, মহা হরষিত চিতে,
মুনিরে করিল অভ্যুত্থান ।
মুনি পরণাম করে, পড়িয়া চরণতলে,
তুলি ব্রহ্মা কৈলা আলিঙ্গন ॥ ২৭৮ ॥

*dekhi brahmā ati byaste, mahā haraṣita cite,*
*munire karila abhyutthāna |*
*muni paraṇāma kare, paṛiẏā caraṇatale,*
*tuli brahmā kailā āliṅgana || 278 ||*

*Word for word:* dekhi brahma — seeing, Brahma; ati vyaste — hastily; maha harashita chite — with great joy at heart; munire karila abhyutthana — rose to greet the sage; muni paranama kare — the sage bows; padiya charana-tale — falling at his feet; tuli brahma kaila alingana — raising him, Brahma embraced him

**278.** Seeing him, Brahma hastily, with great joy at heart,
rose to greet the sage;
the sage bows, falling at his feet;
raising him, Brahma embraced him.

পুছিলা কুশলবাণী, আগমনে ধন্য মানি,
চির-দরশন-অনুরাগে ।
হেন লয় মোর মন, দেখি তোর সুবদন,
রহস্য কহিবে মহাভাগে ॥ ২৭৯ ॥

*puchilā kuśalabāṇī, āgamane dhanya māni,*
*cira-daraśana-anurāge |*
*hena laẏa mora mana, dekhi tora subadana,*
*rahasya kahibe mahābhāge || 279 ||*

*Word for word:* puchhila kushala-vani — he asked of his welfare; agamane dhanya mani — deeming himself blessed by the visit; chira-darashana-anurage — with love long unseen; hena laya mora mana — so my mind tells me; dekhi tora suvadana — seeing your bright face; rahasya kahibe mahabhage — you will tell a secret, fortunate one

**279.** He asked of his welfare, deeming himself blessed by his coming,
with the love of long separation:
"It seems to me, looking at your bright face,
that you, fortunate one, will tell a secret.

তোর মুখোদিত-বাণী, শ্রবণে অমিয়া মানি,
হিয়া জুড়াউক কহ শুনি ।
কৈছন লোকের কথা, কহ প্রভু-গুণগাথা,
কি দেখিলে কি শুনিলে তুমি ॥ ২৮০ ॥

*tora mukhodita-bāṇī, śrabaṇe amiẏā māni,*
*hiẏā juṛāuka kaha śuni |*
*kaichana lokera kathā, kaha prabhu-guṇagāthā,*
*ki dekhile ki śunile tumi || 280 ||*

*Word for word:* tora mukhodita-vani — words from your mouth; shravane amiya mani — I deem nectar to the ear; hiya juduka — let my heart be soothed; kaha shuni — speak, I shall listen; kaichhana lokera katha — what news of the worlds; kaha prabhu-guna-gatha — tell the song of the Lord's virtues; ki dekhile ki shunile tumi — what you have seen and heard

**280.** Words from your mouth are nectar to the ear;
speak — I shall listen; let my heart be soothed:
what news of the worlds? Tell the song of the Lord's virtues —
what have you seen, what have you heard?"

কথা কহে পরিপাটী, নারদের আরভটী,
স্ফুরিত অধর দোলে অঙ্গ ।
বাষ্প-জল-ভরা আঁখি, অরুণ অধর দেখি,
কথারম্ভে দ্বিগুণ আনন্দ ॥ ২৮১ ॥

*kathā kahe paripāṭī, nāradera ārabhaṭī,*
*sphurita adhara dole aṅga |*
*bāṣpa-jala-bharā āṁkhi, aruṇa adhara dekhi,*
*kathārambhe dbiguṇa ānanda || 281 ||*

*Word for word:* katha kahe paripati — he speaks in order; naradera arabhati — with Narada's ardour; sphurita adhara — lips quivering; dole anga — body swaying; bashpa-jala-bhara ankhi — eyes full of tears; aruna adhara dekhi — reddened lips seen; katharambhe dviguna ananda — as he begins, his joy doubles

**281.** In due order Narada tells his story, full of ardour:
his lips quiver, his body sways,
his eyes are full of tears, his lips are red —
as he begins to speak, his joy is doubled:

শুন অদভুত কথা, তুমি সর্বসৃষ্টিকর্তা,
তোর নাম বুলিয়ে ব্রহ্মাণ্ড ।
যুগ-অনুরূপ রূপে, যুগধর্ম করে লোকে,
কলিযুগে পাপ পরচণ্ড ॥ ২৮২ ॥

*śuna adabhuta kathā, tumi sarbasṛṣṭikartā,*
*tora nāma buliẏe brahmāṇḍa |*
*yuga-anurūpa rūpe, yugadharma kare loke,*
*kaliyuge pāpa paracaṇḍa || 282 ||*

*Word for word:* shuna adabhuta katha — hear wondrous news; tumi sarva-srishti-karta — you are the maker of all creation; tora nama — [bearing] your name; bulie brahmanda — I roam the universe (Brahmanda); yuga-anurupa rupe — according to each yuga; yuga-dharma kare loke — people practise the dharma of the age; kali-yuge papa parachanda — in the Kali-yuga sin is fierce

**282.** "Hear wondrous news. You are the maker of all creation;
I roam the universe that bears your name.[^05-1]
According to each yuga people practise the dharma of that yuga,
but in the Kali-yuga sin is rampant.

দ্বাপর-শেষের লোকে, সব দুঃখময় শোকে,
দেখি মোর কলিকে তরাস ।
কাতর হৃদয়ে মরি, গেলুঁ পঁহু বরাবরি,
সুধাইনু পরম সাহসে ॥ ২৮৩ ॥

*dbāpara-śeṣera loke, saba duḥkhamaẏa śoke,*
*dekhi mora kalike tarāsa |*
*kātara hṛdaẏe mari, geluṁ paṁhu barābari,*
*sudhāinu parama sāhase || 283 ||*

*Word for word:* dvapara-sheshera loke — the people at the end of Dvapara; saba duhkhamaya shoke — all in sorrowful grief; dekhi — seeing; mora kalike tarasa — I dread Kali; katara hridaye mari — dying with an anguished heart; gelun panhu barabari — I went straight to the Lord; sudhainu parama sahase — I asked with great boldness

**283.** Seeing the people at the end of Dvapara, all in sorrowful grief,
I dreaded Kali;
with an anguished heart I went straight to the Lord
and asked with great boldness:

কলি পাপময় যুগে, নিস্তার করিবে লোকে,
কহ প্রভু কেমন উপায় ।
ব্রাহ্মণ সে বেদহীন, সর্বলোক ধর্মক্ষীণ,
মোর হিয়ায় এ বড় সংশয় ॥ ২৮৪ ॥

*kali pāpamaẏa yuge, nistāra karibe loke,*
*kaha prabhu kemana upāẏa |*
*brāhmaṇa se bedahīna, sarbaloka dharmakṣīṇa,*
*mora hiẏāẏa e baṛa saṃśaẏa || 284 ||*

*Word for word:* kali papamaya yuge — in the sinful age of Kali; nistara karibe loke — [how] will You deliver the people; kaha prabhu kemana upaya — tell, Lord, by what means; brahmana se vedahina — the brahmanas are without the Vedas; sarvaloka dharma-kshina — in all people dharma has waned; mora hiyaya e bada samshaya — in my heart is this great doubt

**284.** 'In the sinful age of Kali by what means
will You deliver the people? Tell me, Lord:
the brahmanas are without the Vedas, dharma has waned in all —
in my heart is a great doubt.'

শুনিঞা কাতর-বাণী, বোলে পঁহু গুণমণি,
দূর কর হৃদয়ের চিন্তা ।
কলি-লোক নিস্তারিব, নিজ ভক্তি প্রচারিব,
অবতার করিব মো তথা ॥ ২৮৫ ॥

*śuniñā kātara-bāṇī, bole paṁhu guṇamaṇi,*
*dūra kara hṛdaẏera cintā |*
*kali-loka nistāriba, nija bhakti pracāriba,*
*abatāra kariba mo tathā || 285 ||*

*Word for word:* shuniya katara-vani — hearing the piteous words; bole panhu gunamani — the Lord, jewel of virtues, says; dura kara hridayera chinta — put away the anxiety of your heart; kali-loka nistariba — I shall deliver the people of Kali; nija bhakti prachariba — I shall spread devotion to Me; avatara kariba mo tatha — I shall descend there

**285.** Hearing the piteous words, the Lord, jewel of virtues, says:
'Put away the anxiety of your heart:
I shall deliver the people of Kali, I shall spread devotion to Me,
I shall descend there Myself.

দান ব্রত তপ ধর্ম, আর যত যত কর্ম,
সব আরোপিব হরিনামে ।
কলি দোষময় দেখ, এক মহাগুণ লেখ,
মুক্তবন্ধ মোর সঙ্কীর্তনে ॥ ২৮৬ ॥

*dāna brata tapa dharma, āra yata yata karma,*
*saba āropiba harināme |*
*kali doṣamaẏa dekha, eka mahāguṇa lekha,*
*muktabandha mora saṅkīrtane || 286 ||*

*Word for word:* dana vrata tapa dharma — charity, vows, austerity, dharma; ara yata yata karma — and all other works; saba aropiba hari-name — I shall place all in Hari's name; kali doshamaya dekha — see, Kali is full of faults; eka mahaguna lekha — [but] note one great virtue; mukta-bandha mora sankirtane — release from bonds by My sankirtana

**286.** Charity, vows, austerity, dharma and all other works —
all this I shall place in Hari's name;
see, Kali is full of faults, but note one great virtue:
release from bondage — by My sankirtana.[^05-2]

ঘোষণা বোলহ তুমি, শিব-ব্রহ্মা-আদি ভূমি,
সভে জনমহ কলি পাঞা ।
করুণা-বিগ্রহ আমি, জনম লভিব ভূমি,
যুগ-অনুসারে গৌর হঞা ॥ ২৮৭ ॥

*ghoṣaṇā bolaha tumi, śiba-brahmā-ādi bhūmi,*
*sabhe janamaha kali pāñā |*
*karuṇā-bigraha āmi, janama labhiba bhūmi,*
*yuga-anusāre gaura hañā || 287 ||*

*Word for word:* ghoshana bolaha tumi — proclaim; shiva-brahma-adi — Shiva, Brahma and the rest; bhumi — on earth; sabhe janamaha kali pana — all be born when Kali comes; karuna-vigraha ami — I, the embodiment of compassion; janama labhiba bhumi — shall be born on earth; yuga-anusare gaura haina — becoming golden according to the age

**287.** Proclaim: let Shiva, Brahma and the rest
all be born on earth when Kali comes;
I, the embodiment of compassion, shall be born on earth,
becoming golden according to the yuga.'"[^05-3]

*Shubhachhanda, raga pahida; disha: "Glory, glory to the moon Gauranga, risen in Nadia in the age of Kali! — Murchha: — Ah, hear the story of my Lord, whose virtues lit up these three worlds! Ah, hear the story of Gaurangachand! Ah, what is this, ah!"*

এছন শুনিঞা বাণী বিরিঞ্চি ঠাকুর ।
হৃদয়ে রোপিল প্রেম-অমিয়া-অঙ্কুর ॥ ২৮৮ ॥

*echana śuniñā bāṇī biriñci ṭhākura |*
*hṛdaẏe ropila prema-amiẏā-aṅkura || 288 ||*

*Word for word:* echhana shuniya vani — hearing such words; virinchi thakura — lord Brahma; hridaye ropila — planted in his heart; prema-amiya-ankura — a sprout of the nectar of prema

**288.** Hearing such words, lord Brahma
planted in his heart a sprout of the nectar of prema.

গণ্ড পুলকিত আঁখি অশ্রুধারা গলে ।
আনন্দে বিহ্বল ব্রহ্মা মুনি কৈলা কোলে ॥ ২৮৯ ॥

*gaṇḍa pulakita āṁkhi aśrudhārā gale |*
*ānande bihbala brahmā muni kailā kole || 289 ||*

*Word for word:* ganda pulakita — cheeks thrilling; ankhi ashrudhara gale — tears stream from his eyes; anande vihvala brahma — Brahma, overwhelmed with joy; muni kaila kole — embraced the sage

**289.** His cheeks thrill, tears stream from his eyes;
beside himself with joy, Brahma embraced the sage.

বোলয়ে বিরিঞ্চি শুন মহামুনিবর ।
তোর পরসাদে আজি প্রসন্ন অন্তর ॥ ২৯০ ॥

*bolaẏe biriñci śuna mahāmunibara |*
*tora parasāde āji prasanna antara || 290 ||*

*Word for word:* bolaye virinchi — Brahma says; shuna mahamunivara — hear, best of great sages; tora parasade — by your grace; aji prasanna antara — today my heart is clear

**290.** Brahma says: "Hear, best of great sages:
by your grace my heart is made clear today.

বিষয়-বিপাকে সভে মায়াবন্ধে অন্ধ ।
তোর পরসাদে পুনঃ হয় মুক্তবন্ধ ॥ ২৯১ ॥

*biṣaẏa-bipāke sabhe māẏābandhe andha |*
*tora parasāde punaḥ haẏa muktabandha || 291 ||*

*Word for word:* vishaya-vipake — in the snare of worldly objects; sabhe maya-bandhe andha — all are blind in the bonds of maya; tora parasade — by your grace; punah haya mukta-bandha — they are freed from bonds again

**291.** In the snare of worldly things all are blind in the bonds of maya;
by your grace they are freed from their bonds again.

লোক-নিস্তারণ-হেতু তোর মাত্র চিন্তা ।
পুরুব-বৃত্তান্ত কিছু কহি নিজ-বার্তা ॥ ২৯২ ॥

*loka-nistāraṇa-hetu tora mātra cintā |*
*puruba-bṛttānta kichu kahi nija-bārtā || 292 ||*

*Word for word:* loka-nistarana-hetu — for the deliverance of people; tora matra chinta — is your only concern; puruba-vrittanta kichhu — something of the past; kahi nija-varta — I tell, my own story

**292.** You care only for the deliverance of people;
I shall tell you something of the past — about myself.

সনকাদি মুনি যত আমার নন্দনে ।
অন্তর প্রকাশি কিছু কহিল মো স্থানে ॥ ২৯৩ ॥

*sanakādi muni yata āmāra nandane |*
*antara prakāśi kichu kahila mo sthāne || 293 ||*

*Word for word:* sanakadi muni yata — the sages Sanaka and the others; amara nandane — my sons; antara prakashi — opening their hearts; kichhu kahila mo sthane — said something to me

**293.** The sages Sanaka and the others, my sons,
opening their hearts, said to me:

আমারে কহিল—তুমি প্রভু-প্রিয়পুত্র ।
যে কিছু পুছিয়ে তার কহ মোরে সূত্র ॥ ২৯৪ ॥

*āmāre kahila—tumi prabhu-priẏaputra |*
*ye kichu puchiẏe tāra kaha more sūtra || 294 ||*

*Word for word:* amare kahila — they said to me; tumi prabhu-priya-putra — you are the Lord's beloved son; ye kichhu puchhiye — whatever we ask; tara kaha more sutra — tell us its key

**294.** 'You are the Lord's beloved son;
whatever we ask, explain to us its essence.

অচিন্ত্য অব্যয় প্রভু নিত্যানন্দ ব্রহ্ম ।
সূক্ষ্ম সর্বেশ্বরেশ্বর সর্বময় ধর্ম ॥ ২৯৫ ॥

*acintya abyaẏa prabhu nityānanda brahma |*
*sūkṣma sarbeśbareśbara sarbamaẏa dharma || 295 ||*

*Word for word:* achintya — inconceivable; avyaya — imperishable; prabhu — the Lord; nitya-ananda brahma — eternally blissful Brahman; sukshma — subtle; sarveshvareshvara — lord of all lords; sarvamaya — all-pervading; dharma — dharma

**295.** The Lord is inconceivable, imperishable, eternally blissful, He is Brahman,
subtle, lord of all lords, all-pervading, [the ground of] dharma;

অনন্ত নির্গুণ নিরঞ্জন নিরাকার ।
আদি মধ্য অন্ত নাহি এ বুদ্ধি-বিচার ॥ ২৯৬ ॥

*ananta nirguṇa nirañjana nirākāra |*
*ādi madhya anta nāhi e buddhi-bicāra || 296 ||*

*Word for word:* ananta — infinite; nirguna — beyond the gunas; niranjana — spotless; nirakara — formless; adi madhya anta nahi — no beginning, middle or end; e buddhi-vichara — such is the judgment of reason

**296.** infinite, beyond the gunas, spotless, formless,
without beginning, middle or end — so reason judges.[^05-4]

এছন ঠাকুর হঞা পৃথিবীতে জন্ম ।
অজ হঞা জন্মি করে প্রাকৃতের কর্ম ॥ ২৯৭ ॥

*echana ṭhākura hañā pṛthibīte janma |*
*aja hañā janmi kare prākṛtera karma || 297 ||*

*Word for word:* echhana thakura haina — being such a Lord; prithivite janma — birth on earth; aja haina — though unborn; janmi kare — being born, He does; prakritera karma — the acts of ordinary people

**297.** How then, being such a Lord, is He born on earth —
unborn, yet being born, does the deeds of ordinary men?

বৃন্দাবনে রাস কৈল গোপবধূ-সঙ্গে ।
কামিজন যেন কাম-রতি-রসরঙ্গে ॥ ২৯৮ ॥

*bṛndābane rāsa kaila gopabadhū-saṅge |*
*kāmijana yena kāma-rati-rasaraṅge || 298 ||*

*Word for word:* vrindavane rasa kaila — in Vrindavana He held the rasa; gopa-vadhu-sange — with the cowherd wives; kamijana yena — like lustful people; kama-rati-rasa-range — in the play of amorous pleasure

**298.** In Vrindavana He held the rasa with the cowherd wives,
like people given to the play of amorous pleasure.[^05-5]

কি নারী পুরুষ সেই আত্মা সব জনে ।
এছন রমণে তাঁর অসন্তোষ কেনে ॥ ২৯৯ ॥

*ki nārī puruṣa sei ātmā saba jane |*
*echana ramaṇe tāṁra asantoṣa kene || 299 ||*

*Word for word:* ki nari purusha — be they women or men; sei atma saba jane — He is the Self in all; echhana ramane — in such dalliance; tara asantosha kene — why His discontent?

**299.** Be they women or men, He is the Self in all:
why then such dalliance, as though He were not content?

এছন সন্দেহ মোর হৃদয়ে বিশাল ।
তত্ত্ব কহ চতুর্মুখ ঘুচাহ জঞ্জাল ॥ ৩০০ ॥

*echana sandeha mora hṛdaẏe biśāla |*
*tattba kaha caturmukha ghucāha jañjāla || 300 ||*

*Word for word:* echhana sandeha — such a doubt; mora hridaye vishala — is great in my heart; tattva kaha — tell the truth; chaturmukha — Four-faced one; ghuchaha janjala — remove the confusion

**300.** Great is this doubt in my heart;[^05-6]
tell the truth, Four-faced one, clear away the confusion.'

এছন সন্দেহ কথা সনকাদি বৈল ।
শুনিঞা হৃদয়ে মোর বিস্ময় হইল ॥ ৩০১ ॥

*echana sandeha kathā sanakādi baila |*
*śuniñā hṛdaẏe mora bismaẏa haila || 301 ||*

*Word for word:* echhana sandeha katha — such words of doubt; sanakadi baila — Sanaka and the others spoke; shuniya — hearing; hridaye mora vismaya haila — wonder arose in my heart

**301.** When Sanaka and the others expressed such a doubt,
hearing it, I was amazed at heart.

অন্তর-চিন্তায় মোর মলিন বদন ।
মোর অগোচর এই প্রভু-আচরণ ॥ ৩০২ ॥

*antara-cintāẏa mora malina badana |*
*mora agocara ei prabhu-ācaraṇa || 302 ||*

*Word for word:* antara-chintaya — with inner anxiety; mora malina vadana — my face grew dark; mora agochara — beyond my grasp; ei prabhu-acharana — is this conduct of the Lord

**302.** My face darkened with anxiety:
this conduct of the Lord is beyond my grasp.

বেদান্তের পার এই কেবা জানে তত্ত্ব ।
আমা হেন কত ব্রহ্মা আছে শত শত ॥ ৩০৩ ॥

*bedāntera pāra ei kebā jāne tattba |*
*āmā hena kata brahmā āche śata śata || 303 ||*

*Word for word:* vedantera para ei — this is beyond Vedanta; keba jane tattva — who knows the truth; ama hena — like me; kata brahma achhe — how many Brahmas there are; shata shata — hundreds upon hundreds

**303.** This is beyond Vedanta; who knows the truth?
Brahmas like me there are hundreds upon hundreds.

এই মনঃকথা আমি কহিবার বেলে ।
হংসরূপে আসি প্রভু বৈলা হেনকালে ॥ ৩০৪ ॥

*ei manaḥkathā āmi kahibāra bele |*
*haṃsarūpe āsi prabhu bailā henakāle || 304 ||*

*Word for word:* ei manah-katha — this thought; ami kahibara bele — when I was about to speak; hamsa-rupe asi prabhu — coming in the form of Hamsa, the Lord; baila hena-kale — spoke at that moment

**304.** Just as I was about to voice this thought,
at that very moment the Lord came in the form of Hamsa and spoke:

চারি শ্লোকে সমাধান কহিল আমারে ।
সেই সমাধান আমি দিল তা সভারে ॥ ৩০৫ ॥

*cāri śloke samādhāna kahila āmāre |*
*sei samādhāna āmi dila tā sabhāre || 305 ||*

*Word for word:* chari shloke — in four verses; samadhana kahila amare — He gave me the answer; sei samadhana — that answer; ami dila ta sabhare — I gave to them all

**305.** in four verses He gave me the answer,
and that answer I passed on to them all.[^05-7]

সন্তোষ পাইল সেই সব মহাশয় ।
পরিতোষে গেলা যথা যার মনে লয় ॥ ৩০৬ ॥

*santoṣa pāila sei saba mahāśaẏa |*
*paritoṣe gelā yathā yāra mane laẏa || 306 ||*

*Word for word:* santosha paila — were pleased; sei saba mahashaya — all those great souls; paritoshe gela — went away satisfied; yatha yara mane laya — wherever each wished

**306.** All those great souls were pleased
and, satisfied, went wherever each wished.

সেই চতুঃশ্লোকী মোর সব রস-ভাণ্ড ।
তার তত্ত্ব জানে হেন নাহিক ব্রহ্মাণ্ড ॥ ৩০৭ ॥

*sei catuḥślokī mora saba rasa-bhāṇḍa |*
*tāra tattba jāne hena nāhika brahmāṇḍa || 307 ||*

*Word for word:* sei chatuh-shloki — those four verses; mora saba rasa-bhanda — are to me the vessel of all rasa; tara tattva jane hena — one who knows their truth; nahika brahmanda — there is none in the universe

**307.** Those four verses are to me the vessel of all rasa;
there is none in the universe who knows their truth.

কথোদিন রহি ব্যাস নৈমিষ-অরণ্যে ।
সব বিবরিল যত ভারত-পুরাণে ॥ ৩০৮ ॥

*kathodina rahi byāsa naimiṣa-araṇye |*
*saba bibarila yata bhārata-purāṇe || 308 ||*

*Word for word:* kathodina rahi — after some time; vyasa — Vyasa; naimisha-aranye — in the Naimisha forest; saba vivarila — set forth everything; yata bharata-purane — in the Bharata and the Puranas

**308.** Some time later Vyasa, in the Naimisha forest,
set forth all that is in the *Bharata* and the Puranas;

না হৈল শেষ কিছু বলিবার তরে ।
জাড্য না ঘুচিল তবু পড়িল ফাঁপরে ॥ ৩০৯ ॥

*nā haila śeṣa kichu balibāra tare |*
*jāḍya nā ghucila tabu paṛila phāṁpare || 309 ||*

*Word for word:* na haila shesha kichhu — nothing was left; balibara tare — to say; jadya na ghuchila — the heaviness did not lift; tabu padila phanpare — yet he fell into distress

**309.** nothing was left to say, yet the heaviness of heart did not lift,
and he fell into distress.

মূর্চ্ছা পাইল ব্যাসদেব অরণ্য-ভিতরে ।
জানি উপজিল দয়া ঠাকুর-অন্তরে ॥ ৩১০ ॥

*mūrcchā pāila byāsadeba araṇya-bhitare |*
*jāni upajila daẏā ṭhākura-antare || 310 ||*

*Word for word:* murchchha paila vyasadeva — Vyasadeva swooned; aranya-bhitare — in the forest; jani — knowing this; upajila daya — compassion arose; thakura-antare — in the Lord's heart

**310.** Vyasadeva swooned in the forest;
knowing this, the Lord was filled with compassion.

আমাকে ডাকিয়া দিল চারি শ্লোক এই ।
এই পরধন লঞা যাহ ব্যাস ঠাঁই ॥ ৩১১ ॥

*āmāke ḍākiẏā dila cāri śloka ei |*
*ei paradhana lañā yāha byāsa ṭhāṁi || 311 ||*

*Word for word:* amake dakiya — calling me; dila chari shloka ei — He gave these four verses; ei para-dhana lana — taking this supreme treasure; yaha vyasa thain — go to Vyasa

**311.** Calling me, He gave these four verses:
"Take this supreme treasure and go to Vyasa.

ব্যাস নাহি জানে মোর আচরণ-তত্ত্ব ।
এই শ্লোক-অনুসারে করু ভাগবত ॥ ৩১২ ॥

*byāsa nāhi jāne mora ācaraṇa-tattba |*
*ei śloka-anusāre karu bhāgabata || 312 ||*

*Word for word:* vyasa nahi jane — Vyasa does not know; mora acharana-tattva — the truth of My deeds; ei shloka-anusare — following these verses; karu bhagavata — let him compose the Bhagavata

**312.** Vyasa does not know the truth of My deeds;
let him compose the *Bhagavata* following these verses.

সেই ভাগবত তুমি কহিও নারদে ।
তার জিহ্বায় সরস্বতী কহিব শারদে ॥ ৩১৩ ॥

*sei bhāgabata tumi kahio nārade |*
*tāra jihbāẏa sarasbatī kahiba śārade || 313 ||*

*Word for word:* sei bhagavata — that Bhagavata; tumi kahio narade — tell to Narada; tara jihvaya — on his tongue; sarasvati kahiba sharade — Sarasvati, Sharada, will speak

**313.** This *Bhagavata* you shall tell to Narada:
Sarasvati, Sharada, will speak with his tongue."[^05-8]

এতেকে কহিয়ে তুমি শুন মুনিবর ।
যুগে যুগে তুমি মাত্র জীবে দয়া কর ॥ ৩১৪ ॥

*eteke kahiẏe tumi śuna munibara |*
*yuge yuge tumi mātra jībe daẏā kara || 314 ||*

*Word for word:* eteke kahiye — therefore I say; tumi shuna munivara — hear, best of sages; yuge yuge — age after age; tumi matra — you alone; jive daya kara — show mercy to living beings

**314.** Therefore I say: hear, best of sages —
age after age you alone show mercy to living beings.

জীবের নিস্তার-হেতু তুমি মহাজন ।
ভাগবত দিব্য শাস্ত্র নাহি আর ধন ॥ ৩১৫ ॥

*jībera nistāra-hetu tumi mahājana |*
*bhāgabata dibya śāstra nāhi āra dhana || 315 ||*

*Word for word:* jivera nistara-hetu — for the deliverance of beings; tumi mahajana — you are the great soul; bhagavata divya shastra — the Bhagavata, divine scripture; nahi ara dhana — there is no other treasure

**315.** For the deliverance of living beings you are the great soul;
the *Bhagavata* is the divine scripture — there is no other treasure.

নির্বিষয় ভাগবত স্বতন্ত্র পুরুষ ।
না বুঝিঞা শাস্ত্র-জ্ঞান করয়ে মূরুখ ॥ ৩১৬ ॥

*nirbiṣaẏa bhāgabata sbatantra puruṣa |*
*nā bujhiñā śāstra-jñāna karaẏe mūrukha || 316 ||*

*Word for word:* nirvishaya bhagavata — the Bhagavata is free of worldliness; svatantra purusha — an independent Person; na bujhina — not understanding; shastra-jnana karaye murukha — the fool takes it for book-learning

**316.** The *Bhagavata* is untouched by worldliness — it is an independent Person;[^05-9]
not understanding this, the fool takes it for mere book-learning.

হেন ভাগবত-কথা কৃষ্ণ-অবতারে ।
গর্গমুনি বৈল নামকরণের কালে ॥ ৩১৭ ॥

*hena bhāgabata-kathā kṛṣṇa-abatāre |*
*gargamuni baila nāmakaraṇera kāle || 317 ||*

*Word for word:* hena bhagavata-katha — such a statement of the Bhagavata; krishna-avatare — at Krishna's descent; gargamuni baila — Garga Muni spoke; namakaranera kale — at the name-giving ceremony

**317.** Such a statement of the *Bhagavata* about Krishna's descent
Garga Muni made at the name-giving ceremony;[^05-10]

এবে সে স্মরণ হৈল গর্গমুনি-বাণী ।
চারিযুগ-অনুরূপ বরণ-কাহিনী ॥ ৩১৮ ॥

*ebe se smaraṇa haila gargamuni-bāṇī |*
*cāriyuga-anurūpa baraṇa-kāhinī || 318 ||*

*Word for word:* ebe se smarana haila — now I remembered; gargamuni-vani — Garga Muni's words; chari-yuga-anurupa — according to the four yugas; barana-kahini — the account of the colours

**318.** now I have remembered Garga Muni's words,
the account of [the Lord's] colours according to the four yugas.

*So in the* Srimad-Bhagavata *(10.8.13):*

আসন্ বর্ণাস্ত্রয়ো হ্যস্য গৃহ্ণতোঽনুযুগং তনূঃ ।
শুক্লো রক্তস্তথা পীত ইদানীং কৃষ্ণতাং গতঃ ॥ ৩১৯ ॥

*āsan barṇāstraẏo hyasya gṛhṇato'nuyugaṃ tanūḥ |*
*śuklo raktastathā pīta idānīṃ kṛṣṇatāṃ gataḥ || 319 ||*

*Word for word:* asan — there were; varnah trayah — three colours; hi asya — indeed of Him; grihnatah — who accepts; anuyugam — in each yuga; tanuh — bodies; shuklah — white; raktah — red; tatha pitah — and likewise yellow; idanim — now; krishnatam gatah — He has become black (Krishna)

**319.** "Taking bodies yuga after yuga, He had three colours —
white, red and likewise yellow; now He has become dark (Krishna)."[^05-11]

সত্যযুগে শ্বেতবর্ণ লোকে পরচার ।
ত্রেতায় অরুণ-কান্তি যজ্ঞ-নাম তার ॥ ৩২০ ॥

*satyayuge śbetabarṇa loke paracāra |*
*tretāẏa aruṇa-kānti yajña-nāma tāra || 320 ||*

*Word for word:* satya-yuge shvetavarna — in the Satya-yuga white; loke parachara — known among people; tretaya aruna-kanti — in the Treta of rosy lustre; yajna-nama tara — His name is Yajna

**320.** In the Satya-yuga people knew Him as white,
in the Treta as of rosy lustre, and His name was Yajna;

এবে কৃষ্ণবর্ণ এই নন্দের কুমার ।
পরিশেষে পীতবর্ণ হৈব অবতার ॥ ৩২১ ॥

*ebe kṛṣṇabarṇa ei nandera kumāra |*
*pariśeṣe pītabarṇa haiba abatāra || 321 ||*

*Word for word:* ebe krishnavarna — now dark; ei nandera kumara — this son of Nanda; parisheshe — at the last; pitavarna haiba avatara — there will be an avatara of yellow colour

**321.** now this son of Nanda is dark,
and at the last there will be an avatara of yellow colour.[^05-12]

ক্রমভঙ্গ বলি শ্লোকে সন্দেহ যাহার ।
চারিযুগে তিন বর্ণ এ বুদ্ধি তাহার ॥ ৩২২ ॥

*kramabhaṅga bali śloke sandeha yāhāra |*
*cāriyuge tina barṇa e buddhi tāhāra || 322 ||*

*Word for word:* kramabhanga bali — calling it a break in the order; shloke sandeha yahara — whoever doubts the verse; chari-yuge tina varna — three colours in four yugas; e buddhi tahara — such is his understanding

**322.** Whoever doubts the verse, saying that its order is broken,
understands it thus: three colours for four yugas.

শ্বেত রক্ত পীত কৃষ্ণ চারি বর্ণ বহি ।
চারিযুগ বহি আর এক যুগ নাহি ॥ ৩২৩ ॥

*śbeta rakta pīta kṛṣṇa cāri barṇa bahi |*
*cāriyuga bahi āra eka yuga nāhi || 323 ||*

*Word for word:* shveta rakta pita krishna — white, red, yellow, dark; chari varna vahi — four colours; chari-yuga vahi — apart from four yugas; ara eka yuga nahi — there is no other yuga

**323.** White, red, yellow, dark — these are four colours,
and the yugas are four, there are no others.

নহে বা বিচারি দেখ গৌর কোন্ যুগে ।
আস্তে ব্যস্তে কহিলে সন্দেহ নাহি ভাগে ॥ ৩২৪ ॥

*nahe bā bicāri dekha gaura kon yuge |*
*āste byaste kahile sandeha nāhi bhāge || 324 ||*

*Word for word:* nahe ba vichari dekha — or else consider; gaura kon yuge — in which yuga is the golden one; aste vyaste kahile — speaking hastily; sandeha nahi bhage — the doubt does not break

**324.** Otherwise consider: in which yuga is [the Lord] golden?
Speaking hastily, one will not dispel the doubt.

ইহার বিচার কিছু কহি তাহা শুন ।
ভক্তজনেরে ইহা বুঝাব এখন ॥ ৩২৫ ॥

*ihāra bicāra kichu kahi tāhā śuna |*
*bhaktajanere ihā bujhāba ekhana || 325 ||*

*Word for word:* ihara vichara kichhu — some discussion of this; kahi taha shuna — I tell; listen; bhakta-janere — to the devotees; iha bujhaba ekhana — I shall now explain this

**325.** I shall say a little about this — listen:
I shall now explain it to the devotees.

একাদশে এই কথা কহে ভাগবতে ।
রাজা প্রশ্ন কৈল করভাজন-মুনিতে ॥ ৩২৬ ॥

*ekādaśe ei kathā kahe bhāgabate |*
*rājā praśna kaila karabhājana-munite || 326 ||*

*Word for word:* ekadashe — in the eleventh [canto]; ei katha kahe bhagavate — the Bhagavata says this; raja prashna kaila — the king asked; karabhajana-munite — the sage Karabhajana

**326.** The *Bhagavata* speaks of this in the eleventh canto:
the king asked the sage Karabhajana.[^05-13]

*So in the* Srimad-Bhagavata *(11.5.19); the king said:*

কস্মিন্ কালে স ভগবান্ কিং বর্ণঃ কীদৃশো নৃভিঃ ।
নাম্না বা কেন বিধিনা পূজ্যতে তদিহোচ্যতাম্ ॥ ৩২৭ ॥

*kasmin kāle sa bhagabān kiṃ barṇaḥ kīdṛśo nṛbhiḥ |*
*nāmnā bā kena bidhinā pūjyate tadihocyatām || 327 ||*

*Word for word:* kasmin kale — at what time; sa bhagavan — that Bhagavan; kim varnah — of what colour; kidrishah — of what form; nribhih — by men; namna va kena — by what name; vidhina — by what rite; pujyate — is worshipped; tat iha uchyatam — tell this here

**327.** "At what time, of what colour and form is that Bhagavan,
by what name and by what rite is He worshipped by men? Tell us this."

কোন্ কালে ভগবান্ কোন্ বর্ণ ধরে ।
কি নাম তাহার সেই হৈল কোন্ কালে ॥ ৩২৮ ॥

*kon kāle bhagabān kon barṇa dhare |*
*ki nāma tāhāra sei haila kon kāle || 328 ||*

*Word for word:* kon kale bhagavan — at what time Bhagavan; kon varna dhare — takes what colour; ki nama tahara — what is His name; sei haila kon kale — at what time

**328.** At what time does Bhagavan take what colour,
what is His name, at what time [did He appear];

কোন্ কালে কোন্ ধর্ম কেমন মানুষ ।
কোন্ বিধি পূজা করে কিসে বা সন্তোষ ॥ ৩২৯ ॥

*kon kāle kon dharma kemana mānuṣa |*
*kon bidhi pūjā kare kise bā santoṣa || 329 ||*

*Word for word:* kon kale — at what time; kon dharma — what dharma; kemana manusha — what kind of people; kon vidhi puja kare — by what rite they worship; kise ba santosha — what pleases [Him]

**329.** at what time what dharma, what kind of people,
by what rite do they worship, what pleases [Him]?

*Sri Karabhajana said (11.5.20–22):*

কৃতং ত্রেতা দ্বাপরঞ্চ কলিরিত্যেষু কেশবঃ ।
নানাবর্ণাভিধাকারো নানৈব বিধিনেজ্যতে ॥ ৩৩০ ॥

*kṛtaṃ tretā dbāparañca kalirityeṣu keśabaḥ |*
*nānābarṇābhidhākāro nānaiba bidhinejyate || 330 ||*

*Word for word:* kritam treta dvaparam cha kalih — Krita, Treta, Dvapara and Kali; iti eshu — in these; keshavah — Keshava; nana-varna-abhidha-akarah — of various colours, names and forms; nana eva vidhina — by various rites; ijyate — is worshipped

**330.** "In the Krita, Treta, Dvapara and Kali yugas Keshava
is of various colours, names and forms, and is worshipped by various rites.

কৃতে শুক্লশ্চতুর্বাহুর্জটিলো বল্কলাম্বরঃ ।
কৃষ্ণাজিনোপবীতাক্ষান্ বিভ্রদ্দণ্ডকমণ্ডলূ ॥ ৩৩১ ॥

*kṛte śuklaścaturbāhurjaṭilo balkalāmbaraḥ |*
*kṛṣṇājinopabītākṣān bibhraddaṇḍakamaṇḍalū || 331 ||*

*Word for word:* krite — in Krita; shuklah — white; chatur-bahuh — four-armed; jatilah — with matted locks; valkala-ambarah — clad in bark; krishna-ajina — black deerskin; upavita — sacred thread; akshan — rosary; bibhrat — bearing; danda-kamandalu — staff and waterpot

**331.** In the Krita He is white, four-armed, with matted locks, clad in bark,
bearing a black deerskin, sacred thread, rosary, staff and waterpot.

মনুষ্যাস্তু তদা শান্তা নির্বৈরাঃ সুহৃদঃ সমাঃ ।
যজন্তি তপসা দেবং শমেন চ দমেন চ ॥ ৩৩২ ॥

*manuṣyāstu tadā śāntā nirbairāḥ suhṛdaḥ samāḥ |*
*yajanti tapasā debaṃ śamena ca damena ca || 332 ||*

*Word for word:* manushyah tu tada — people then; shantah — peaceful; nirvairah — without enmity; suhridah — friendly; samah — even-minded; yajanti — worship; tapasa — with austerity; devam — God; shamena cha damena cha — with control of mind and senses

**332.** People then are peaceful, without enmity, friendly, even-minded;
they worship God with austerity and control of mind and senses."

রাজাকে কহিছে মুনি শুন সাবধানে ।
সত্য-আদি-যুগে লোক পূজয়ে কেমনে ॥ ৩৩৩ ॥

*rājāke kahiche muni śuna sābadhāne |*
*satya-ādi-yuge loka pūjaẏe kemane || 333 ||*

*Word for word:* rajake kahichhe muni — the sage tells the king; shuna savadhane — listen attentively; satya-adi-yuge — in Satya and the other yugas; loka pujaye kemane — how people worship

**333.** The sage says to the king: "Listen attentively
to how people worship in the Satya and the other yugas.

সত্যযুগে শ্বেতবর্ণ হংস নাম ধরে ।
চতুর্বাহু তপোধর্ম জটা-বাকল পরে ॥ ৩৩৪ ॥

*satyayuge śbetabarṇa haṃsa nāma dhare |*
*caturbāhu tapodharma jaṭā-bākala pare || 334 ||*

*Word for word:* satya-yuge shvetavarna — in the Satya-yuga white; hamsa nama dhare — bears the name Hamsa; chaturbahu — four-armed; tapo-dharma — austerity [His] dharma; jata-vakala pare — wears matted locks and bark

**334.** In the Satya-yuga He is white and bears the name Hamsa;
four-armed, His dharma is austerity, He wears matted locks and bark,

দণ্ড কমণ্ডলু কৃষ্ণসার-উপবীত ।
শান্ত নির্বৈর সম লোকের চরিত ॥ ৩৩৫ ॥

*daṇḍa kamaṇḍalu kṛṣṇasāra-upabīta |*
*śānta nirbaira sama lokera carita || 335 ||*

*Word for word:* danda kamandalu — staff, waterpot; krishnasara-upavita — antelope skin and sacred thread; shanta nirvaira sama — peaceful, without enmity, even; lokera charita — is the character of people

**335.** staff, waterpot, antelope skin and sacred thread;
and people are by nature peaceful, without enmity, even-minded."

*So (11.5.24–25):*

ত্রেতায়াং রক্তবর্ণোঽসৌ চতুর্বাহুস্ত্রিমেখলঃ ।
হিরণ্যকেশস্ত্রয্যাত্মা স্রুক্স্রুবাদ্যুপলক্ষণঃ ॥ ৩৩৬ ॥

*tretāẏāṃ raktabarṇo'sau caturbāhustrimekhalaḥ |*
*hiraṇyakeśastrayyātmā sruksrubādyupalakṣaṇaḥ || 336 ||*

*Word for word:* tretayam — in Treta; rakta-varnah asau — He is red; chatur-bahuh — four-armed; tri-mekhalah — with a triple girdle; hiranya-keshah — golden-haired; trayi-atma — the soul of the three Vedas; sruk-sruva-adi-upalakshanah — marked by sacrificial ladles and the like

**336.** "In the Treta-yuga He is red, four-armed, with a triple girdle,
golden-haired, the soul of the three Vedas, marked by sacrificial ladles and the like.

তং তদা মনুজা দেবং সর্বদেবময়ং হরিম্ ।
যজন্তি বিদ্যয়া ত্রয্যা ধর্মিষ্ঠা ব্রহ্মবাদিনঃ ॥ ৩৩৭ ॥

*taṃ tadā manujā debaṃ sarbadebamaẏaṃ harim |*
*yajanti bidyaẏā trayyā dharmiṣṭhā brahmabādinaḥ || 337 ||*

*Word for word:* tam tada — Him then; manujah — men; devam — God; sarva-deva-mayam harim — Hari, comprising all the gods; yajanti — worship; vidyaya trayya — by the knowledge of the three Vedas; dharmishthah — the righteous; brahma-vadinah — learned in the Veda

**337.** Then people, righteous and learned in the Veda, worship Him —
God Hari, who comprises all the gods — by the knowledge of the three Vedas."

সেই প্রভু ত্রেতাযুগে রক্তবর্ণ ধরে ।
চারি বাহু ত্রিমেখল স্রুক্-স্রুব করে ॥ ৩৩৮ ॥

*sei prabhu tretāyuge raktabarṇa dhare |*
*cāri bāhu trimekhala sruk-sruba kare || 338 ||*

*Word for word:* sei prabhu — that Lord; treta-yuge — in the Treta-yuga; raktavarna dhare — takes red colour; chari bahu — four arms; trimekhala — triple girdle; sruk-sruva kare — sacrificial ladles in hand

**338.** That Lord in the Treta-yuga takes a red colour:
four arms, a triple girdle, sacrificial ladles in His hands,

তপ্ত-হাটক-কেশ শিরের উপরে ।
সর্বদেবময় প্রভু আপে যজ্ঞ করে ॥ ৩৩৯ ॥

*tapta-hāṭaka-keśa śirera upare |*
*sarbadebamaẏa prabhu āpe yajña kare || 339 ||*

*Word for word:* tapta-hataka-kesha — hair like molten gold; shirera upare — on His head; sarvadevamaya prabhu — the Lord comprising all gods; ape yajna kare — Himself performs sacrifice

**339.** on His head hair like molten gold;
the Lord who comprises all the gods Himself performs sacrifice.

ত্রয়ী-বেদ আত্মা তাঁর নাম ধরে যজ্ঞ ।
বেদ-বিধিমতে পূজা করে ধর্মবিজ্ঞ ॥ ৩৪০ ॥

*traẏī-beda ātmā tāṁra nāma dhare yajña |*
*beda-bidhimate pūjā kare dharmabijña || 340 ||*

*Word for word:* trayi-veda atma tara — the three Vedas are His soul; nama dhare yajna — He bears the name Yajna; veda-vidhi-mate — by Vedic rules; puja kare — worship; dharma-vijna — those versed in dharma

**340.** The three Vedas are His soul; He bears the name Yajna;
those versed in dharma worship Him by the rules of the Vedas.

*So of the Dvapara (11.5.27–28, 31):*

দ্বাপরে ভগবান্ শ্যামঃ পীতবাসা নিজায়ুধঃ ।
শ্রীবৎসাদিভিরঙ্কৈশ্চ লক্ষণৈরুপলক্ষিতঃ ॥ ৩৪১ ॥

*dbāpare bhagabān śyāmaḥ pītabāsā nijāẏudhaḥ |*
*śrībatsādibhiraṅkaiśca lakṣaṇairupalakṣitaḥ || 341 ||*

*Word for word:* dvapare — in Dvapara; bhagavan shyamah — Bhagavan is dark; pita-vasah — in yellow garments; nija-ayudhah — with His weapons; shrivatsa-adibhih ankaih cha — with the Shrivatsa and other marks; lakshanaih — with signs; upalakshitah — distinguished

**341.** "In the Dvapara Bhagavan is dark, in yellow garments, with His own weapons,
distinguished by the Shrivatsa and other marks.

তং তদা পুরুষং মর্ত্যা মহারাজোপলক্ষণম্ ।
যজন্তি বেদতন্ত্রাভ্যাং পরং জিজ্ঞাসবো নৃপ ॥ ৩৪২ ॥

*taṃ tadā puruṣaṃ martyā mahārājopalakṣaṇam |*
*yajanti bedatantrābhyāṃ paraṃ jijñāsabo nṛpa || 342 ||*

*Word for word:* tam tada purusham — Him, the Person, then; martyah — mortals; maharaja-upalakshanam — bearing the marks of a great king; yajanti — worship; veda-tantrabhyam — by the Vedas and tantras; param — the Supreme; jijnasavah — seekers of knowledge; nripa — O king

**342.** Then mortals seeking knowledge worship Him, the Supreme Person,
bearing the marks of a great king, by the Vedas and tantras, O king.

ইতি দ্বাপর উর্বীশ স্তুবন্তি জগদীশ্বরম্ ।
নানাতন্ত্রবিধানেন কলাবপি তথা শৃণু ॥ ৩৪৩ ॥

*iti dbāpara urbīśa stubanti jagadīśbaram |*
*nānātantrabidhānena kalābapi tathā śṛṇu || 343 ||*

*Word for word:* iti — thus; dvapare — in Dvapara; urvisha — O lord of the earth; stuvanti — they praise; jagad-ishvaram — the Lord of the world; nana-tantra-vidhanena — by the rules of various tantras; kalau api — in Kali also; tatha shrinu — hear how

**343.** Thus in the Dvapara, O lord of the earth, they praise the Lord of the world
by the rules of various tantras; and how [they praise Him] in Kali — hear."[^05-14]

দ্বাপরেতে শ্যামবর্ণ ধরে ভগবান্ ।
শ্রীবৎস কৌস্তুভ অঙ্গে পীত পরিধান ॥ ৩৪৪ ॥

*dbāparete śyāmabarṇa dhare bhagabān |*
*śrībatsa kaustubha aṅge pīta paridhāna || 344 ||*

*Word for word:* dvaparete — in Dvapara; shyamavarna dhare bhagavan — Bhagavan takes a dark colour; shrivatsa kaustubha ange — Shrivatsa and Kaustubha on His body; pita paridhana — yellow garments

**344.** In the Dvapara Bhagavan takes a dark colour:
the Shrivatsa and Kaustubha on His body, yellow garments;

মহারাজ-রাজাধিপ-লক্ষণ বিরাজে ।
ভাগ্যবান্ লোক তাঁরে বেদ-তন্ত্রে যজে ॥ ৩৪৫ ॥

*mahārāja-rājādhipa-lakṣaṇa birāje |*
*bhāgyabān loka tāṁre beda-tantre yaje || 345 ||*

*Word for word:* maharaja-rajadhipa-lakshana — the marks of a great king, sovereign of kings; viraje — shine; bhagyavan loka — fortunate people; tare veda-tantre yaje — worship Him by Vedas and tantras

**345.** the marks of a great king, sovereign of kings, shine on Him;
fortunate people worship Him by the Vedas and tantras.

এইমত প্রতিযুগে যুগ-অবতার ।
যে যুগে যে ধর্ম লোকে করয়ে আচার ॥ ৩৪৬ ॥

*eimata pratiyuge yuga-abatāra |*
*ye yuge ye dharma loke karaẏe ācāra || 346 ||*

*Word for word:* eimata — thus; pratiyuge — in every yuga; yuga-avatara — the yuga-avatara; ye yuge ye dharma — in each yuga its dharma; loke karaye achara — people practise

**346.** Thus in every yuga [comes] the yuga-avatara,
and people practise the dharma of their yuga.

সত্য ত্রেতা দ্বাপর তিন যুগ গেল ।
শ্বেত রক্ত আর কৃষ্ণ বরণ হইল ॥ ৩৪৭ ॥

*satya tretā dbāpara tina yuga gela |*
*śbeta rakta āra kṛṣṇa baraṇa haila || 347 ||*

*Word for word:* satya treta dvapara — Satya, Treta, Dvapara; tina yuga gela — three yugas have passed; shveta rakta ara krishna — white, red and dark; barana haila — were the colours

**347.** Satya, Treta and Dvapara — three yugas have passed,
and the colours were white, red and dark.

[^05-1]: *Brahmanda*, literally "Brahma's egg", the universe.
[^05-2]: Cf. *Bhag.* 12.3.51: "O king, Kali is an ocean of faults, but it has one great virtue: by chanting of Krishna one is freed from bondage and attains the Supreme."
[^05-3]: Cf. below (vv. 319–321 and 349): according to the *Bhagavata*, the Lord in each yuga takes a form of its own colour; in Kali, golden.
[^05-4]: This is the reasoning of the Kumaras, who formerly adhered to the impersonal Brahman (cf. *Bhag.* 3.15.43: the fragrance of the tulasi at the Lord's feet turned them to bhakti). In the Vaishnava understanding "beyond the gunas" and "formless" mean "free of material qualities and material form": the Lord has an eternal spiritual form.
[^05-5]: This is the doubt of the Kumaras, not the author's assertion. Parikshit voices the same doubt (*Bhag.* 10.33.27–28), and Shukadeva answers it (10.33.29–37): the rasa is the purest prema, not mundane passion; the Lord is self-satisfied and dwells as the Witness in the hearts of the gopis and their husbands. Bhaktisiddhanta stresses that the love of the gopis is the highest form of prema, free from all lust.
[^05-6]: A has "my heart", although many Kumaras are asking; so in both editions.
[^05-7]: In the *Bhagavata* the Lord in the form of Hamsa answers the Kumaras' question about detaching the mind from sense objects (11.13), while the four verses that are the essence of the *Bhagavata* (2.9.32–35) the Lord reveals to Brahma before creation. Lochana Dasa joins these accounts.
[^05-8]: In the *Bhagavata* (2.9; 1.5–1.7) Brahma passes on what he heard to Narada, and Narada instructs the dejected Vyasa.
[^05-9]: Cf. *Bhag.* 1.3.43: when Krishna departed to His abode, the *Bhagavata* rose like the sun for the people of Kali who have lost their sight.
[^05-10]: *Bhag.* 10.8: Garga Muni, the priest of the Yadus, gives names to Krishna and Balarama in Nanda's house.
[^05-11]: Garga Muni's words at Krishna's name-giving. The Gaudiya acharyas (*Chaitanya-charitamrita*, Adi 3.36–40) take "yellow" (*pita*) as the golden form in which Krishna appears in the Kali-yuga as Sri Chaitanya, and "now He has become Krishna" as the appearance of Krishna Himself, the original Lord. Further on (portion 06) Lochana Dasa discusses this verse at length.
[^05-12]: "At the last" (*parisheshe*), i.e. in the Kali-yuga, the last of the four; so Lochana Dasa takes the "yellow" colour of the verse.
[^05-13]: In the *Bhagavata* (11.2–11.5) King Nimi (Videha) questions the nine sage-yogendras; Karabhajana answers about the yuga-avataras.
[^05-14]: Verses 11.5.29–30 (the hymn of the Dvapara) the author does not cite. The verse on Kali (11.5.32) is quoted at the beginning of portion 06.

---

# Sutra-khanda, part 6 (portion 06)

*Brahma continues: the Lord in the Kali-yuga is the golden Gaura of whom the* Bhagavata *speaks (11.5.32); explanation of the words "krishna-varna" and "sangopanga", of Garga Muni's verse on the four colours and of the word "tatha"; Krishna is not a yuga-avatara but Bhagavan Himself, and in the Dvapara and the Kali it is He Himself who descends; testimonies of the* Gita, *the "Thousand Names" and the* Bhavishya-purana; *the greatness of the Kali-yuga and of sankirtana*

তিন যুগে তিন বর্ণ কহি দিল মুনি ।
সাবধানে শুন কলিযুগের কাহিনী ॥ ৩৪৮ ॥

*tina yuge tina barṇa kahi dila muni |*
*sābadhāne śuna kaliyugera kāhinī || 348 ||*

*Word for word:* tina yuge tina varna — three colours in three yugas; kahi dila muni — the sage named; savadhane shuna — hear attentively; kali-yugera kahini — the account of the Kali-yuga

**348.** Of the three colours in three yugas the sage has told;
now hear attentively the account of the Kali-yuga.

*So in the* Srimad-Bhagavata *(11.5.32):*

কৃষ্ণবর্ণং ত্বিষাকৃষ্ণং সাঙ্গোপাঙ্গাস্ত্রপার্ষদম্ ।
যজ্ঞৈঃ সঙ্কীর্তনপ্রায়ৈর্যজন্তি হি সুমেধসঃ ॥ ৩৪৯ ॥

*kṛṣṇabarṇaṃ tbiṣākṛṣṇaṃ sāṅgopāṅgāstrapārṣadam |*
*yajñaiḥ saṅkīrtanaprāẏairyajanti hi sumedhasaḥ || 349 ||*

*Word for word:* krishna-varnam — uttering "Krishna" (dark in colour); tvisha akrishnam — not dark in lustre; sa-anga-upanga-astra-parshadam — with limbs, sub-limbs, weapons and associates; yajnaih — by sacrifices; sankirtana-prayaih — consisting chiefly of sankirtana; yajanti — worship; hi — indeed; sumedhasah — the intelligent

**349.** "Him who utters [the name] 'Krishna' but is not dark in lustre,[^06-1] with His limbs, sub-limbs, weapons and associates,
the intelligent worship with sacrifices consisting chiefly of sankirtana."

কৃষ্ণ এই দুই বর্ণ আছয়ে যাহাতে ।
কৃষ্ণবর্ণ নাম তার কহে ভাগবতে ॥ ৩৫০ ॥

*kṛṣṇa ei dui barṇa āchaẏe yāhāte |*
*kṛṣṇabarṇa nāma tāra kahe bhāgabate || 350 ||*

*Word for word:* krishna ei dui varna — these two syllables "Krish-na"; achhaye yahate — in whom are; krishna-varna nama tara — His name is "krishna-varna"; kahe bhagavate — says the Bhagavata

**350.** He in whom there are these two syllables, "Krish-na",
the *Bhagavata* calls "krishna-varna".[^06-2]

কান্তিতে অকৃষ্ণ সেই শুন সর্বজন ।
গোরা গোরা বলি গাই এই সে কারণ ॥ ৩৫১ ॥

*kāntite akṛṣṇa sei śuna sarbajana |*
*gorā gorā bali gāi ei se kāraṇa || 351 ||*

*Word for word:* kantite akrishna sei — by lustre He is not dark; shuna sarvajana — hear, all; gora gora bali gai — we sing "Gora, Gora"; ei se karana — this is the reason

**351.** And in lustre He is "not dark" — hear, everyone:
this is why we sing, "Gora, Gora!"

সাঙ্গোপাঙ্গ অস্ত্র যত পারিষদ আর ।
সভার সহিত প্রভু কৈলা অবতার ॥ ৩৫২ ॥

*sāṅgopāṅga astra yata pāriṣada āra |*
*sabhāra sahita prabhu kailā abatāra || 352 ||*

*Word for word:* sanga-upanga — limbs and sub-limbs; astra — weapons; yata parishada ara — and all the associates; sabhara sahita — together with all; prabhu kaila avatara — the Lord descended

**352.** With His limbs, sub-limbs, weapons and all His associates —
with all of them the Lord descended.

অঙ্গে বলরাম বলি তেঞি কহি সাঙ্গ ।
উপ-অঙ্গ আভরণ তেঞি সে উপাঙ্গ ॥ ৩৫৩ ॥

*aṅge balarāma bali teñi kahi sāṅga |*
*upa-aṅga ābharaṇa teñi se upāṅga || 353 ||*

*Word for word:* ange balarama bali — Balarama is called a limb; tenji kahi sanga — therefore I say "with limbs"; upa-anga abharana — the lesser limbs are ornaments; tenji se upanga — therefore "with sub-limbs"

**353.** Balarama is called the limb — so I say "with limbs";
the lesser limbs are ornaments — so "with sub-limbs".[^06-3]
